products.title: Bucephalandra Kedagang Japan Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
A Kedagang selected in Japan. Bucephalandra sp. 'Kedagang Japan' carries narrow, slightly rippled leaves with a metallic sheen running green through blue into faint violet. Selected from Japanese stock, where Buce breeding has pushed hardest on colour. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format.

What You'll Receive

  • One sealed 4-inch Vitro Culture® tissue culture bag
  • Approximately 4 small plantlets grown in sterile nutrient gel
  • 100% free from snails, algae, pesticides and pathogens
  • Rinse the gel away and separate the plantlets before planting

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Kedagang Japan Buce
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. 'Kedagang Japan'
  • Also known as — Buce Japan Kedagang, Buce, Bucep
  • Origin — Japanese selection; the genus is native to Borneo
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, on wood or stone
  • Mature height — 2–4 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Stronger light brings out the metallic tones
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it improves growth and colour
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Not required. Attaches to hardscape
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed — suits paludariums and Wabi-Kusa
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • Kedagang is the plant, the suffix is the selection. You'll see Kedagang Red, Kedagang Mini and Kedagang Japan — all the same plant type, differing in colour and leaf size. Buy on the look you want rather than assuming they're separate species.
  • The metallic sheen is structural, not pigment — it shifts with viewing angle and lighting, and photographs rarely do it justice.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Glue or tie it to rock or wood; buried rhizomes rot.
  • Rinse the gel off completely and separate the four plantlets before attaching, or it feeds algae in the first weeks.
  • Farm-raised, not wild-collected. All the Bucephalandra we carry is farm-grown, and much of it is raised from tissue culture rather than collected from Borneo.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Bucephalandra Care Guide.

Notes

  • Pictures shown are for reference only. Actual plant size, shape, and colour may vary depending on growth conditions. This Vitro Culture® bag is sealed for freshness — please follow proper sterilization and acclimation procedures upon opening.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Myriophyllum sp. Roraima Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Milfoil that colours. Myriophyllum sp. 'Roraima' grows the fine feathery whorls the genus is known for, but runs orange through reddish-brown under strong light instead of staying green — an unusual thing in a milfoil, and the reason to choose it over the common green species. From the Roraima region of Brazil. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® (tissue culture) format.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Myriophyllum sp. 'Roraima' Vitro Culture® cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®, available in convenient pack sizes:

  • 1 Bag: One 4-inch Vitro Culture® bag containing many small plantlets ready for separation and planting.
  • 5 Bags: Five 4-inch Vitro Culture® bags containing many small plantlets per bag for larger aquascaping projects.
  • 10 Bags: Ten 4-inch Vitro Culture® bags containing many small plantlets per bag, ideal for large aquariums, propagation, or aquascape layouts.

Each 4-inch bag contains multiple healthy plantlets grown in sterile nutrient gel, allowing you to separate and plant many individual stems throughout your aquarium.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Roraima Milfoil
  • Scientific name — Myriophyllum sp. 'Roraima'
  • Also known as — Red Milfoil, Roraima Watermilfoil
  • Origin — Roraima, Brazil
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — 4-inch bag of small plantlets
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Very fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Light intensity is what produces the orange and red
  • CO₂ — Not required. It grows without injection, though colour and density improve with it
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.0
  • Substrate — Not required. It feeds mainly from the water column
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • Very fast means very fast. This is among the quickest growers in the genus and will reach the surface and shade everything beneath it if left alone. Trim on a schedule rather than when it looks untidy — that is the difference between a dense bush and a bare-stemmed mess.
  • Dose the water column. Milfoil absorbs through its foliage rather than its roots, so liquid macro and micronutrients matter far more than root tabs. Washed-out colour is usually an iron or trace shortfall.
  • Rinse the gel off and separate the plantlets before planting, spacing them an inch apart. Fine whorled foliage shades itself badly when planted as a clump.
  • Trim and replant the tops. It branches readily from below the cut, so repeated topping is how a few stems become a dense group.
  • Plant it as a block against green neighbours. The warm colour reads as an accent, and a single stem among green plants just looks lost.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Myriophyllum (Milfoil) Care Guide.

Notes

  • Appearance, size, and coloration may vary depending on growing conditions and season. Plants may arrive in their emersed (farm-grown) form and will transition to their submerged aquarium form after planting.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Alternanthera Pink Sunset
products.body_html:
Looking for pink without the bulk? Alternanthera reineckii 'Pink Sunset' is a mutation of Alternanthera reineckii that our nursery first introduced to the United States in 2021. It reads like Alternanthera reineckii 'Rosanervig' at a glance, but the stems are finer and the leaves noticeably narrower — a lighter, more delicate texture in the same colour range.

What You’ll Receive

Choose from our selection of fresh, nursery-grown Alternanthera reineckii ‘Pink Sunset’:

  • Loose Fresh-Cut Plants: Approximately 6 unrooted, freshly trimmed stems.
  • Fresh Cut Bunched: About 6 stems, neatly bundled with foam and a plant weight, without root.
  • Potted Plants: Around 6 fresh-cut stems, without root in a net pot with rock wool.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pink Sunset Alternanthera
  • Scientific name — Alternanthera reineckii 'Pink Sunset'
  • Also known as — AR Pink Sunset
  • Origin — Cultivar; introduced by Aquarium Plants Factory nursery (U.S.A., 2021)
  • Placement — Midground
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Colour intensity tracks light
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5, soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed, with more compact leaves
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Narrower leaves change how it plants. Standard Alternanthera reineckii makes broad blocks of colour. Pink Sunset's finer stems let you use pink as an accent inside a group rather than as a wall of it.
  • The colour lives on the leaf underside. Position it where the light rakes across rather than straight down, and the magenta actually shows.
  • Trim and replant tops rather than letting stems run tall. Repeated topping is what turns three stems into a dense group.
  • It feeds both at the roots and from the water column, so root tabs plus regular dosing outperform either alone.
  • Some fading and leaf drop during acclimation is normal; new growth returns to colour once light and nutrients are steady.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Alternanthera Care Guide.

Notes

  • Some initial leaf melt or slight colour fading may occur during shipping or acclimation. This is normal — new growth will quickly regain vivid pink hues under stable lighting and nutrient conditions.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Alternanthera Reineckii 'Super Magenta'
products.body_html:
Want magenta rather than plain red? Alternanthera reineckii 'Super Magenta' runs deeper into pink and purple than standard AR, and holds it further down the stem. It is the strongest colour contrast you can put next to a green background without resorting to a difficult plant.

What You’ll Receive

Enhance your aquarium with our fresh, high-quality plants, available in three convenient formats:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Includes approximately 5+ loose, fresh-cut stems without roots – perfect for custom placement
  • Fresh-Cut Bunched: About 5+ fresh-cut stems bundled with foam and plant weight – ideal for easy setup
  • Fresh-Cut Potted: Approximately 5+ fresh-cut stems potted in rockwool and net pot – ready to anchor and grow

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Super Magenta Alternanthera, also known as Scarlet Temple, Purple Telanthera
  • Scientific name — Alternanthera reineckii 'Super Magenta'
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species is South American
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, kept low by trimming
  • Shipped size — Approx. 5+ fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in untrimmed
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Higher light intensifies the magenta
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5, soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Required. Root and water column feeder
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Trim hard and often. Left alone it reaches for the surface and goes bare at the base; topped regularly it stays a dense magenta block, which is the whole point of this variety.
  • Colour needs iron and lean nitrate together. Strong light alone with a heavily fed tank gives you a large green plant.
  • Replant the trimmed tops into the stand rather than keeping bare lower stems — tops root fast and colour up immediately.
  • Plant stems a little apart. Packed tight, the inner stems lose colour first and then drop their leaves.
  • For the standard species at the same care level, see Alternanthera reineckii.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Alternanthera Care Guide.

Notes

  • Photos shown are representative samples. Plants may arrive with slight variation in size or colour depending on growth stage. Unless otherwise stated, aquatic plants may arrive in emersed form and are not guaranteed to be pest- or pesticide-free.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Alternanthera Rosanervig
products.body_html:
Colour drawn in lines, not blocks. Alternanthera reineckii 'Rosanervig' carries a network of pale pink veins across leaves that shift from green through pink to deep magenta — so the plant reads as pattern up close and as a pink mass from across the room. The veining is the distinguishing feature; standard reineckii is solid-coloured.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as loose Fresh-cut plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Fresh-cut plants | Approx. 6 stems, loose fresh-cut stems without root
  • Bunched plants | Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems without root, bundled with foam, and lead weight
  • Potted plants | Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems without root, potted with net pot and rockwool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pink Vein Alternanthera
  • Scientific name — Alternanthera reineckii 'Rosanervig'
  • Also known as — Telanthera Rosanervig, Rosanervig Scarlet Temple, Alternanthera cardinalis Variegata
  • Origin — South America (species range)
  • Placement — Midground
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Colour intensity tracks light
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5, soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Pale veins are the cultivar, not a deficiency. New buyers sometimes dose iron harder thinking the light veining is chlorosis. It isn't — that pattern is what you paid for.
  • The colour sits on the leaf underside as much as the top. Position it where light rakes across rather than straight down.
  • Trim and replant the tops rather than letting stems run tall; repeated topping builds a dense group.
  • It feeds at the roots and from the water column — root tabs plus regular dosing outperform either alone.
  • Also available as Alternanthera Rosanervig Mini for smaller tanks, and Pink Sunset for a finer-stemmed version of the same colour range.

products.title: Alternanthera Reineckii
products.body_html:
The benchmark red stem plant. Alternanthera reineckii — Scarlet Temple, or simply AR — grows broad leaves with green tops and deep red-to-purple undersides on upright bushy stems. It is the plant most people mean when they say they want red in a planted tank, and unlike many red stems it will colour without pressurised CO₂.

What You’ll Receive

Enhance your aquarium with our versatile selection of high-quality aquatic plants, available in three convenient formats:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Includes approximately 6+ loose, fresh-cut stems without roots. Perfect for flexible planting arrangements.
  • Fresh-Cut Bunched: Approximately 6+ fresh-cut stems without roots, bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy placement.
  • Fresh-Cut Potted: About 6+ fresh-cut stems without roots, securely potted in a net pot with rockwool, ensuring stability and healthy growth.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Scarlet Temple
  • Scientific name — Alternanthera reineckii
  • Also known as — AR, Telanthera rosefolia
  • Origin — South America
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6+ fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Colour intensity tracks light
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Red on a budget of light, not CO₂. Rotala and Ludwigia reds usually want gas and nitrate management. AR colours mainly on light intensity and iron, which puts real red within reach of a medium-light tank.
  • The colour sits on the leaf undersides. Position it where light rakes across the group rather than straight down.

products.title: Bacopa caroliniana 'Variegated'
products.body_html:
Rare variegation without the difficulty. Bacopa caroliniana 'Variegated' marbles the thick, rounded leaves of classic Lemon Bacopa with creamy white — and keeps the parent's hardiness. Crush a leaf and it still carries the faint lemon scent the species is named for.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as loose fresh-cut plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Fresh-cut plants: Approximately 6 loose, fresh-cut stems.
  • Bunched plants: Approximately 6 fresh-cut plants bundled with foam and a plant weight.
  • Potted plants: Approximately 6 fresh-cut plants with a net pot and rockwool.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Variegated Lemon Bacopa
  • Scientific name — Bacopa caroliniana 'Variegated'
  • Also known as — Bacopa amplexicaulis 'Variegated', Variegated Bacopa Carolina
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species is native to the southeastern United States
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium. Brighter light sharpens the variegation
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Variegated but not fragile. Most white-marbled plants are slow, demanding things. Bacopa caroliniana is one of the toughest stems in the hobby and the variegated form keeps that — rare looks on a plant that tolerates a beginner's tank.
  • It can revert. Plain green shoots may appear and, because they photosynthesise better, will gradually take over. Trim reverted stems out as you spot them.
  • It grows slowly for a Bacopa, so it holds its place in a scape instead of needing weekly trimming.
  • Trim and replant tops to build a group; cuttings root readily.
  • Space stems an inch apart so light reaches the lower leaves. For the plain green original, see Bacopa Caroliniana.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Bacopa caroliniana care guide.

Notes

  • Pictures are not the actual plants you will receive, but a sample representation. Unless specific, we don't guarantee aquatic plants will be free of pests, pesticides, grow emerged, or submerge.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Hygrophila Pinnatifida 'UK' Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
The redder pinnatifida. Hygrophila pinnatifida 'UK' — short for Uttara Kannada, the district in Karnataka it was collected from — carries more deeply lobed leaves and a stronger pull towards red than the common Goa form. Same creeping, hardscape-attaching habit; more colour. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format.

What You'll Receive

  • 1 sealed Vitro Culture® bag (4 inch) containing approx. 3-4 healthy young plants in liquid/gel agar.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pinnatifida 'UK'
  • Scientific name — Hygrophila pinnatifida 'Uttara Kannada'
  • Also known as — Hygrophila pinnatifida UK, Red Pinnatifida
  • Origin — Uttara Kannada, Karnataka, in the Western Ghats of India
  • Placement — Midground; attaches to driftwood and stone
  • Shipped size — Approx. 3-4 tissue-cultured plantlets, roughly 1-2 in
  • Mature height — 4–10 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Low to medium. It grows in low light; the red needs stronger light
  • CO₂ — Recommended for best colour and compact form
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5, soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Not required if attached to hardscape; nutrient substrate if planted
  • Growth habit — Rheophyte. Creeping and branching; roots onto wood and stone
  • Propagation — Cuttings — stem cuttings and lateral shoots

Grower's Notes

  • 'UK' is the one to buy for colour. The widely sold Goa form runs olive to bronze; this collection reddens more readily under the same conditions. If you have grown standard pinnatifida and wanted more red from it, this is the answer rather than more light.
  • Pinholes in older leaves mean potassium. Pinnatifida shows a potassium shortfall before anything else in the tank does. Dosing clears it within a few weeks — it is not a pest or a disease.
  • Tie it to wood rather than burying it. Attached, it roots into the surface and creeps outward, which is the habit worth having. Buried deep in substrate the lower stem rots.
  • Trimming decides the shape — left alone it runs horizontally, topped repeatedly it bushes upward.
  • Separate the plantlets and rinse the gel off completely before attaching, or it feeds algae in the first weeks.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Hygrophila Pinnatifida Care Guide.

Notes

  • Colors and appearance may vary based on tank conditions. Tissue culture plants should be rinsed thoroughly to remove growing gel before planting. Photos shown are for reference and represent mature growth under ideal conditions.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Ludwigia Glandulosa (Peruensis)
products.body_html:
Want burgundy rather than scarlet? Ludwigia glandulosa runs deep wine-red to purple on narrow lance-shaped leaves held on stiff upright stems. It is one of the darker reds available, and it grows straight up with almost no branching — which makes it unusually easy to place.

You may know it as Ludwigia peruensis. That is a trade name — see the note below.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as loose fresh-cut plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approx. 6 individual loose-cut stems without root.
  • Bunched Plants: Approx. 6 stems without root, bundled with foam and plant weight.
  • Potted Plants: Approx. 6 stems without root, potted in rockwool and a net pot.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Ludwigia Peruensis, also known as Cylindricfruit Primrose-Willow
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia glandulosa
  • Also known as — Ludwigia peruensis, Ludwigia perennis, Ludwigia cylindrica (all misapplied)
  • Origin — Southeastern United States
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Why several names?

This plant has been sold as Ludwigia peruensis and Ludwigia perennis for years, and both names are still in wide use. Neither is correct — the plant is Ludwigia glandulosa, a species from the wetlands of the southeastern United States, not from Peru.

You are buying the same plant you have always known as Peruensis, correctly named.

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Intensity decides whether you get wine-red or olive-green
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root and water column feeder, hungry for iron
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • It barely branches on its own. Stems grow straight up with minimal side shoots until you cut the main stem — then lateral shoots form. If you want a dense stand rather than isolated poles, topping is not optional.
  • In lower light the leaves go olive-green with red undersides, which is a two-toned effect worth having in its own right. The wine-red only appears under strong light.
  • It sheds lower leaves when light is insufficient. Bare stems near the substrate mean light isn't reaching them, not a nutrient problem.
  • Iron and steady micronutrients matter more here than for most Ludwigia.
  • Often confused with Ludwigia senegalensis, which carries a visible vein pattern this one lacks.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Ludwigia Care Guide.

Notes

  • Pictures shown are sample representations and not the exact plants you will receive. Unless otherwise specified, we do not guarantee aquatic plants will be free of pests or pesticides, nor whether they are grown emersed or submerged.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Monosolenium Tenerum (Pellia)
products.body_html:
Thicker than moss, and that is the point. Monosolenium tenerum — Pellia — is a liverwort that grows broad ribbon-like fronds rather than fine filaments, forming dense dark green cushions with real substance. It gives a texture nothing else in a planted tank offers, and it does it in low light with no CO₂.

What You’ll Receive

  • Loose Portion: small portion of Monosolenium tenerum, approx. 2" x 2" (5 cm x 5 cm)
  • Ready for Use: Can be tied to rocks, tucked into crevices, or allowed to carpet over time

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pellia
  • Scientific name — Monosolenium tenerum
  • Also known as — Pellia Moss, Round Pellia
  • Origin — East Asia
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, on rock or wood
  • Shipped size — Loose portion, approx. 2" x 2"
  • Mature height — 1–2 in
  • Suits — 5 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Bright light mostly feeds algae on a plant this slow
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Not required. Feeds from the water column
  • Growth habit — Fully aquatic. Does not grow emersed
  • Propagation — Fragmentation — split a cushion and re-tie the pieces

Grower’s Notes

  • It has no roots and no grip — you must tie it down. Unlike Java Moss, Pellia is brittle and heavy and will not attach itself. Use thread, hairnet or mesh over rock, and expect to leave it several months before it holds. Dropped loose on the substrate it simply drifts apart.
  • Keep the light modest. Slow growth means algae settles faster than the plant replaces tissue, and algae inside a dense Pellia cushion cannot be cleaned out.
  • Give it flow. Water moving through the cushion keeps detritus from packing into the centre and rotting.
  • Split and re-tie rather than trimming. Fragments grow into new cushions, so one portion becomes several over a year.
  • Shrimp and fry take shelter in it readily — the dense structure is better cover than fine mosses provide.

Notes

  • Photos shown are sample representations. Actual plant portions may vary in size and density. Unless noted, plants may arrive in emersed or submerged form and are not guaranteed to be pest- or pesticide-free.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Cyperus Helferi
products.body_html:
Want grass that isn't a Vallisneria? Cyperus helferi grows long, narrow, bright green blades from a central rosette — a true sedge rather than an eelgrass, so it stays as a defined clump instead of running across the tank. The leaves move constantly with the flow.

What You’ll Receive

Enhance your aquarium with our fresh, high-quality rosette plants, available in convenient formats:

  • Loose Bare-Root Plants: Includes approximately 1–2 individual bare-root plants, offering flexibility in placement and arrangement.
  • Rooted Bunched Plants: Approximately 1–2 rooted plants, bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy positioning.
  • Rooted Potted Plants: Includes approximately 1–2 rooted plants, securely potted in rockwool and a net pot to ensure stability and effortless integration into your aquascape.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Cyperus Helferi, also known as Helfer's Umbrella Grass
  • Scientific name — Cyperus helferi
  • Origin — Thailand and Myanmar
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium. Stronger light keeps growth dense and upright
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it produces longer leaves with it
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Strong root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Grows well emersed in paludariums
  • Propagation — Side shoots from the base

Grower’s Notes

  • It clumps rather than spreads. Unlike Vallisneria, which runs across the substrate and colonises, Cyperus stays where you plant it and thickens from the base. That makes it far easier to control in a designed layout.
  • Plant it where there is flow. The long flexible blades move with current, and that motion is most of what you are buying.
  • Feed at the roots. It is a strong root feeder and grows short and pale in inert gravel.
  • Propagate by separating side shoots once they have their own roots.
  • It often arrives compressed and pale from packing. New leaves come through within a couple of weeks.

Want to go deeper? Read our guide to the Best Background Plants for Your Planted Aquarium.

Notes

  • Live plants may appear slightly compressed or lighter in colour upon arrival due to shipping. With proper care, Cyperus helferi will quickly recover, sending out new leaves and developing into a graceful, full plant.

products.title: Cryptocoryne Retrospiralis Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Tall, ribbon-like leaves that twist along their length. Cryptocoryne retrospiralis is one of the few crypts that works as a background plant — it gives a planted tank vertical movement without the trimming a stem plant demands. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format.

What You'll Receive

  • 1x Cryptocoryne Retrospiralis Vitro Culture® — grown in 4-inch bag
  • Yields approx. 3–4 healthy young plants ready for planting

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Retrospiralis Crypt, also known as Spiral Water Trumpet
  • Scientific name — Cryptocoryne retrospiralis
  • Origin — India
  • Placement — Background
  • Mature height — 10-16 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it speeds establishment
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.5-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs under the crown.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rosette; also grows emersed, so it suits paludariums
  • Propagation — Runners

Grower's Notes

  • A background plant that does not need cutting. Stem plants reach the surface and then need weekly trimming. Retrospiralis grows to height and stops, which is the entire argument for using a crypt at the back of a low-maintenance tank.
  • Crypt melt is expected and is not failure. Tissue culture plantlets shed their emersed leaves as they convert to submersed growth. Leave the roots undisturbed — new leaves come from the crown within three to six weeks.
  • Plant the crown at substrate level. Bury the roots and leave the growing point exposed. A buried crown rots from the centre.
  • Feed the roots and give it depth. A tall crypt needs a deep, well-fed substrate to anchor and fuel 16 inches of leaf. Root tabs or aquasoil; two inches of substrate minimum.
  • It spreads by runner. Once settled it sends up new plants around the mother — leave space behind it and the stand thickens on its own over a year or two.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Cryptocoryne Care Guide.

Notes

Like many Cryptocoryne species, Cryptocoryne retrospiralis may undergo a temporary "crypt melt" when adapting to a new aquarium environment. This is a normal process. Once established, new growth will emerge and the plant will stabilize.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Ludwigia Super Red Mini | Bulk Pack
products.body_html:
Red without a CO₂ cylinder. Ludwigia Super Red Mini holds deep crimson under strong light alone, where most red stem plants fade to green — and its compact leaves stay in proportion in a way full-size Ludwigia does not. This is the bulk pack: 50, 100 or 200 fresh-cut stems for filling a background or stocking a shop tank in one go.

What You'll Receive

Supplied as fresh-cut stems without roots. Once planted in aquarium substrate, they naturally develop roots.

  • 50 Stems Pack — fresh-cut loose stems
  • 100 Stems Pack — fresh-cut loose stems
  • 200 Stems Pack — fresh-cut loose stems

Stems are typically 4–6+ inches long, depending on seasonal growth and harvesting conditions.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Super Red Mini Ludwigia
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia palustris 'Super Red'
  • Also known as — Ludwigia sp. 'Super Red Mini', Super Red Ludwigia
  • Origin — Cultivated compact form
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Fresh-cut stems, 4–6+ in, no roots
  • Mature height — 4–10 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — High. Light intensity is what sets the depth of red
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required. It colours up without injection, just more slowly
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.0
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • Plant stems individually, not in the bundle they arrive in. Space them roughly an inch apart. Bunched together the lower stems shade out and rot, which is the usual reason a large planting thins from the bottom.
  • Buy the volume rather than waiting for it. A dense red group is made by planting many stems close together, not by waiting for a few to bush out — which is the whole case for a bulk pack over a single portion.
  • Trim the tops and replant the cuttings. They colour faster than the stumps regrow, and repeated topping is how the group thickens.
  • Iron and a fed substrate matter more than CO₂ here. Washed-out colour is usually a micronutrient shortfall, not a carbon one.
  • Expect a transition. Emersed-grown stems arrive greener and may drop some lower leaves as they convert to submerged growth — new growth from the tips is what to judge it on.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Ludwigia Care Guide.

Notes

  • Plants are supplied as fresh-cut stems without roots. Pictures shown are sample representations; actual plants may vary slightly in size, colouration, and leaf shape depending on growing conditions. Some plants may transition from emersed to submerged growth after planting, which is normal.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Bucephalandra Skeleton King
products.body_html:
Veins you can actually see. Bucephalandra sp. 'Skeleton King' carries a pronounced skeletal vein pattern across leaves that run deep green through blue and purple — structure and colour at once, where most Buce offer only colour. From the fast-flowing streams of Borneo.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as Bare-root Plants, Bunched Plants or Potted Plants:

  • Bare-root Plants: Approximately 1-2 loose plants
  • Bunched Plants: Approximately 1-2 plants bundled with a plant weight for easy placement.
  • Potted Plants: Approximately 1-2 plants potted in rockwool and a net pot for secure growth and easy placement.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Skeleton King Buce
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. 'Skeleton King'
  • Also known as — Bucephalandra kishii, Buce, Bucep
  • Origin — Borneo
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, on wood or stone
  • Mature height — 2–4 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Too much light brings algae onto slow-growing leaves
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it improves growth and colour
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5, soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Not required. Attaches to hardscape
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower’s Notes

  • Veining is not variegation. The pale skeletal pattern is vein structure showing through, not missing chlorophyll — so unlike white-marbled plants, Skeleton King is as easy as any ordinary Buce.
  • Give it flow. Bucephalandra come from fast streams and hold their colour better where water moves across the leaves.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Glue or tie it to rock or wood; buried rhizomes rot.
  • Growth is measured in months, which is why Buce holds its shape in a scape for years without trimming.
  • Divide with a clean blade, keeping a few leaves and some roots per section.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Bucephalandra Care Guide.

Notes

  • Pictures are not the actual plants you will receive, but a sample representation. Unless specific, we don't guarantee aquatic plants will be free of pests, pesticides, grow emerged, or submerge.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Cabomba Furcata
products.body_html:
Fine, feathery whorls in pink to reddish-purple — the most delicate texture of any red stem plant, and the reason it's worth the trouble. It is genuinely demanding: high light and pressurized CO₂ are what keep it from unravelling.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as loose Fresh-cut plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Fresh-cut plants: Approx. 6 stems, loose fresh-cut stems without root
  • Bunched plants: Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems without root, bundled with foam, and lead weight
  • Potted plants: Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems without root, potted with net pot and rockwool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Red Cabomba, Fanwort
  • Scientific name — Cabomba furcata
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — High
  • CO₂ — Required
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–6.8
  • Feeding — Water column
  • Propagation — Cuttings

Grower’s Notes

  • This is the least forgiving red stem in common cultivation. Without strong light and pressurized CO₂ the whorls thin, the stems go bare from the bottom, and it falls apart within weeks.
  • It wants soft, acidic water. Above pH 7 it struggles regardless of how good the light and CO₂ are.
  • Plant stems individually, an inch or so apart. Bunched together they shade each other and rot in the middle.
  • Stable conditions matter more than rich ones. It sheds whorls after water changes that swing temperature or chemistry sharply.

Notes

  • Photos are for reference; colour and density vary considerably with lighting, CO₂ and water chemistry.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

With its delicate, feathery leaves and stunning pink, reddish-purple hues, this plant creates a beautiful contrast against green foliage, enhancing the overall aesthetic of your aquascape.

products.title: Cabomba Aquatica
products.body_html:
The classic fanwort, in plain green. Cabomba aquatica opens each leaf into a flat fan of fine segments arranged in pairs along the stem — a soft, feathery texture that catches water movement and gives fry somewhere to hide. Easier to keep than the red Cabomba species, and faster.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as submerged fresh-cut plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:
  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approx. 6 stems, loose fresh-cut plants
  • Bunched Plants: Approx. 6 fresh-cut plants bundled with foam and lead weight
  • Potted Plants: Approx. 6 fresh-cut plants with net pot and rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Green Cabomba
  • Scientific name — Cabomba aquatica
  • Also known as — Fanwort, Giant Cabomba
  • Origin — South America
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Under weak light the stems stretch and shed lower leaves
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.0
  • Substrate — Not required. Feeds mainly from the water column
  • Growth habit — True aquatic. Does not grow emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Green Cabomba is the forgiving one. The red and magenta species in this genus demand high light and CO₂ to hold colour and drop leaves the moment conditions slip. C. aquatica just grows — the same fan texture, far less argument.
  • Handle it as little as possible. Cabomba stems shed leaves where they're gripped; plant them once, by the bare lower stem.
  • Bottom leaves dropping means light isn't reaching them. Trim the tops and replant rather than letting stems get leggy.
  • It feeds from the water, not the substrate, so liquid dosing does more here than root tabs.
  • Some melting after shipping is normal for the genus. New growth from healthy stems follows within a week or two.

Want to go deeper? Read our guide to growing Cabomba plants.

Notes

  • Cabomba species can be delicate during shipping and acclimation. Some initial melting or leaf drop may occur, but healthy stems will regrow once established.

products.title: Cryptocoryne Parva Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Want a foreground carpet that never needs trimming? Cryptocoryne parva is the smallest true Crypt in the hobby — short green rosettes that spread by runner into a neat low carpet, and grow slowly enough that you can leave them alone for months. This is the sterile tissue culture format, free of snails and algae.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as a Tissue Culture Plants with vitamin liquid/gel
  • Packaging May Vary! To be sent in either in vitro bag or cup
  • Bag / Cup size: Approx. 2.5 x 2.5 inches
  • Sustainable growth Crypt species
  • Tissue Culture Technology | 100% Free from Snail, Algae, Pathogen, and Bacteria plus Extended Shelf Life on all in Vitro Plants

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Parva Crypt, Crypt Parva
  • Scientific name — Cryptocoryne parva
  • Origin — Sri Lanka
  • Placement — Foreground
  • Mature height — 1–3 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required! One of the very few carpets that works in a low-tech tank
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.5–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Substrate runners

Grower’s Notes

  • Patience is the whole job. Parva is the slowest carpeting plant we sell — a full foreground takes the better part of a year. In exchange it holds its shape without trimming and lasts for years.
  • Divide the cup into small clumps and plant them with a little space between crowns. Packed tight, they shade each other before they spread.
  • Expect it to melt after planting. Crypts drop their leaves on a change of conditions, then regrow from the roots over two to four weeks. Leave it alone through that.
  • Feed at the roots. In inert gravel it survives but never builds the dense carpet you bought it for.
  • Place it once. Crypts melt again every time they are moved, and Parva is slow enough that a second melt costs months.
  • Rinse the gel off completely before planting or it clouds water and feeds algae in the first weeks.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Cryptocoryne Care Guide.

Notes

products.title: Bolbitis Difformis | Bulk Pack
products.body_html:
Fine, lace-like fronds on a plant that stays under six inches. Bolbitis heteroclita 'Difformis' — Mini Bolbitis — gives the texture of a full-size water fern at nano scale. This is the bulk pack, for covering a whole piece of hardscape or a bonsai tree at once.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Bolbitis heteroclita 'Difformis' cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®.

Each portion consists of approximately one bare-root plant with around 6 healthy leaves.

  • 5 Pack: 5 individual bare-root portions (approximately 6 leaves per portion)
  • 10 Pack: 10 individual bare-root portions (approximately 6 leaves per portion)
  • 20 Pack: 20 individual bare-root portions (approximately 6 leaves per portion)

For best results, attach each plant to driftwood or rocks with aquarium-safe glue or thread, allowing the rhizomes to naturally anchor over time.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Mini Bolbitis, also known as Philippine Bolbitis, Lace Bolbitis
  • Scientific name — Bolbitis heteroclita 'Difformis'
  • Origin — Philippines
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, on wood or stone
  • Mature height — 3-6 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Low to medium. Bright light means algae on slow-growing fronds
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it fills out faster with it
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Not required. Epiphyte — tie or glue the rhizome to hardscape and never bury it.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious; also suits high-humidity terrariums
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • Buy coverage, do not wait for it. Mini Bolbitis is slow enough that filling a large piece of wood from one plant takes years. Twenty portions spread across the hardscape look established immediately — that is the whole case for the bulk pack.
  • Give it flow. This is a rheophyte from shaded Philippine streams, and moderate current keeps the fine fronds clean and moving. In still water detritus settles into the foliage and stays there.
  • Space the portions. Each rhizome needs water movement around it. Where rhizomes press together, debris collects and rot starts at the contact points.
  • Expect a transition. It is grown emersed, so some of the fronds it arrives with will die back as it converts to submerged growth. Leave it alone — new fronds follow.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Attach with cotton thread or a spot of gel glue; the roots grip the wood themselves within a couple of months.

Comparing our Bolbitis: the full-size African species is Bolbitis Heudelotii (8-14 in), and the parent species of this cultivar is Bolbitis Heteroclita (6-10 in).

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Bolbitis Difformis Care Guide.

Notes

Pictures are representative samples only. Live aquatic plants are natural products and may vary in size, color, and fullness depending on season and growing conditions. Bolbitis heteroclita 'Difformis' is commonly grown emersed and may experience a normal transition period as it adapts to submerged aquarium conditions.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

  • Common name — Mini Bolbitis, also known as Philippine Bolbitis, Lace Bolbitis
  • Scientific name — Bolbitis heteroclita 'Difformis'

  • Placement — Foreground to midground, on wood or stone

products.title: Anacharis
products.body_html:
New tank battling algae, or a pond that needs oxygenating? Anacharis is the workhorse. It grows fast enough to strip nitrate before algae can use it, tolerates cold water down to 60°F, and asks for nothing but light — no CO₂, no substrate, no fuss.

What You’ll Receive

You’ll receive approximately 6 fresh Anacharis stems in the format of your choice:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Loose, freshly trimmed stems
  • Bunched Plants: Fresh-cut stems bundled with foam and lead weight
  • Potted Plants: Fresh-cut stems planted in rock wool inside a net pot

All plants are submerged-grown and hand-selected for health and quality.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Anacharis, Brazilian Waterweed, Elodea
  • Scientific name — Egeria densa
  • Placement — Background, or floating as an oxygenator
  • Mature height — 12–24 in and beyond
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner. Close to unkillable in the right state
  • Light — Low to medium is plenty
  • CO₂ — Not required! It grows fast enough without
  • Water — 60–82°F · pH 6.5–8.5, and it handles hard alkaline water easily
  • Feeding — Root and water column
  • Propagation — Cuttings; snap a stem and replant it

Grower’s Notes

  • It works planted or floating. Floating stems grow fastest and strip the most nitrate, which is why it is the classic new-tank and pond plant — planting it is optional.
  • It handles cold. At 60°F it keeps growing when tropical stems stall, making it one of the few plants suited to unheated tanks and outdoor ponds.
  • Trim and replant the tops. Lower stems go bare as they age; cut the healthy top few inches and discard the base rather than waiting for it to refill.
  • Brittle on arrival is normal. Stems snap easily in transit — every fragment with a node will root and grow, so plant the pieces rather than binning them.

Notes

  • Photos are for reference; stem length and leaf density vary with lighting and growing conditions.

products.title: Vallisneria Contortionist
products.body_html:
Want fine spirals at background height? Vallisneria 'Contortionist' twists its blades along their full length while growing upright to 10–20 inches. Of our three twisted Vals it has the narrowest blade, so the spirals read as fine threads rather than broad ribbons.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as Bare-root Plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Bare-root plants | approx. 2-3 loose, bare-root plants
  • Bunched plants | approx. 2-3 rooted plants with foam, and lead weight
  • Potted plants | approx. 2-3 rooted plants with net pot and rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Contortionist Val, also known as Twisted Val
  • Scientific name — Vallisneria 'Contortionist'
  • Origin — Cultivated form
  • Placement — Background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 2-3 plants, roughly 5-10 in
  • Mature height — 10–20 in
  • Suits — 20 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Brighter light tightens the twist
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.5–8.0. Tolerates hard, alkaline water well
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — sand or soil suits it, with root tabs in inert gravel
  • Growth habit — Fully aquatic

Grower’s Notes

  • Plant the crown at the substrate line, never below it. A buried crown rots — the usual reason a new Val fails in the first fortnight.
  • Feed at the roots. In inert gravel it survives but barely spreads; root tabs are what turn three plants into a stand.
  • Don't trim the tops to control height. Cut Val leaves brown at the cut and stay that way — remove whole leaves at the base instead.
  • Runners travel fast. Pull unwanted plantlets by hand rather than cutting, and expect to thin it every month or two.
  • Sand or soil suits it better than coarse gravel, which the runners struggle to travel through.

Choosing between our twisted Vallisneria

products.title: American Frogbit
products.body_html:
Miniature lily pads that need no planting. Limnobium spongia — American Frogbit — floats round, glossy leaves on the surface with a curtain of fine roots trailing beneath. Native to North America, undemanding, and one of the few floaters that looks deliberate rather than weedy.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as a small portion – approx. 1–2 individual plants

Plant Profile

  • Common name — American Frogbit
  • Scientific name — Limnobium spongia
  • Origin — North America
  • Placement — Free-floating on the surface
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required. It takes CO₂ from the air
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.5–7.5
  • Substrate — Not required
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed on wet margins
  • Propagation — Runners — daughter plants form on side stolons

Grower’s Notes

  • Keep the leaves dry on top. Frogbit hates water landing on its leaves — condensation from a tight lid or spray from a filter return makes the tops rot. An open top or a small gap under the lid solves it, and it's the single most common reason Frogbit fails.
  • The long root curtain is the point. It gives shrimp and fry cover and pulls nutrients straight out of the water column.
  • Surface flow packs it into corners. Aim filter returns downward or add a floating ring.
  • Thin it regularly — daughter plants form fast and a sealed surface starves plants below of light.
  • Compare with Amazon Frogbit: similar habit, larger leaves, tropical rather than North American.

Notes

  • As a floating plant, American Frogbit may spread quickly in nutrient-rich water. Regular thinning may be required to maintain light penetration for plants below.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Azolla (Fairy Moss)
products.body_html:
Want surface cover that works as a nutrient sponge? Azolla is a floating fern with tiny overlapping leaves that form a soft mat across the water. It shades out algae, strips nitrate fast, and turns red or bronze under strong light or cool weather.

What You’ll Receive

Our Azolla is sold by portion size and packed in resealable bags. The dimensions below refer to the approximate bag size, not the coverage area after the plants are released into your aquarium or pond.

Portion Size Approx. Bag Size Suggested Count Notes
Small 2" × 2" 20+ Great starter portion for nano aquariums and small ponds.
Medium 3" × 3" 80+ Ideal for medium aquariums and water gardens.
Large 4" × 4" 320+ Best value for large aquariums, ponds, and rapid propagation.

Please Note:

  • Plant counts are approximate since Azolla plants naturally vary in size.
  • Azolla is extremely small and reproduces rapidly under suitable growing conditions, so the number of plants will increase over time.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Fairy Moss, Water Fern, Mosquito Fern
  • Scientific name — Azolla caroliniana
  • Placement — Floating
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium to high. Strong light is what turns it red
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 65–85°F · pH 5.5–7.5
  • Substrate — Not required. Feeds entirely from the water column
  • Propagation — Fragmentation

Grower’s Notes

  • Keep the surface calm. Azolla will not tolerate strong agitation or spray — water sitting on the fronds rots them. Aim filter outflow below the surface or fence the plants off from the turbulence.
  • Thin it weekly. It doubles quickly and a closed mat shades everything below, including your other plants. Scoop out a third at a time.
  • Red colour comes from bright light and cool water, not fertiliser. In a dim warm tank it stays green.
  • It fixes nitrogen through a symbiotic cyanobacterium in its leaves, which is why it grows so fast in water most plants find lean.

Want to go deeper? Read our guide to the Best Floating Plants for Freshwater Aquariums.

Notes

  • Azolla grows rapidly and may require regular thinning in well-lit or nutrient-rich environments. Not recommended for tanks with strong surface agitation or high flow.

featured_image.alt: One of the notable features of Azolla is its unique growth habit. It forms small floating clusters or mats on the water's surface, creating a green carpet-like appearance. The plant consists of tiny, scale-like leaves that are densely packed together, providing a visually appealing texture.

products.title: Ludwigia Red Skeleton
products.body_html:
Want something almost nobody else has? Ludwigia 'Red Skeleton' is a rare variegated mutation — red stems, red leaf undersides, and green upper leaves veined with yellow in a skeleton pattern that looks drawn on. We were the first aquatic plant nursery in the United States to release it.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as Fresh-cut Plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Fresh-cut plants | approx. 6 stems, loose fresh-cut plants without root
  • Bunched plants | approx. 6 fresh-cut plants without root, bundle with foam, and lead weight
  • Potted plants | approx. 6 fresh-cut plants without root, potted with net pot and rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Red Skeleton Ludwigia
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia sp. 'Red Skeleton'
  • Origin — A variegated mutation of Ludwigia repens 'Rubin'
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 6–14 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — High. In low light the leaves stay green and the pattern fades
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.0
  • Substrate — Required. Root and water column feeder
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Variegated plants are harder than their plain parents. The yellow-veined tissue carries less chlorophyll, so this plant photosynthesises less efficiently than standard Rubin and is less tolerant of poor light, unstable CO₂ or neglect. Rate it Advanced regardless of how easy Ludwigia repens is.
  • The mutation is stable. Offspring consistently inherit the variegated genes, so cuttings come true rather than reverting to plain Rubin.
  • Colour and pattern both track light. Under high light it turns deep red with the skeleton veining pronounced; under low light it stays green and the effect largely disappears.
  • Trim and replant the tops. Bare lower stems rarely refill well enough to be worth keeping on a plant this slow to build.
  • Buy it as a group, not a single stem. The skeleton veining is a fine detail that only reads from a distance when several stems are planted together.

Often confused with Ludwigia sp. 'Atlantis', which is a different mutation — that one comes from Ludwigia repens rather than 'Rubin'.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Ludwigia Care Guide.

Notes

  • Pictures are not the actual plants you will receive, but a sample representation. Colour and variegation vary considerably with lighting and nutrients.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Rotala Wallichii
products.body_html:
The finest-textured red stem in the hobby. Rotala wallichii grows needle-thin leaves in dense whorls, so a healthy group reads as a soft pink cloud rather than a set of stems. It is also one of the least forgiving — it wants high light, CO₂ and iron, and it tells you immediately when any of the three slips.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as loose fresh-cut plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Fresh-cut Plants: Approx. 6 individual, loose stems without roots
  • Bunched Plants: Approx. 6 stems without roots, bundled with foam and a lead weight
  • Potted Plants: Approx. 6 stems without roots, potted in rockwool and 2-inch net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Rotala Wallichii
  • Scientific name — Rotala wallichii
  • Also known as — Whorly Rotala, Mayaca-leaf Rotala
  • Origin — Southeast Asia
  • Placement — Midground to background, in dense groups
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — High. Non-negotiable for both colour and form
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.0. Prefers soft, acidic water
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Iron is what turns it pink. Light and CO₂ get you healthy growth; a dedicated iron-rich micronutrient dose is what produces the colour this plant is bought for. Without it, expect a fine green plant.
  • Plant a dozen stems, not three. Wallichii looks thin and weedy as individual stems and only works as a mass — that's why the format sells in sixes and why buying two portions is usually the right call.
  • It sheds lower leaves fast in shade. Trim the tops, replant them, discard the bare stumps rather than waiting for regrowth.
  • It reacts to instability before other plants do. If wallichii starts dropping leaves, check CO₂ consistency before anything else — it works as an early warning for the whole tank.
  • Arriving green is normal. Colour develops over several weeks under your lighting, not in the shipping box.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Rotala Care Guide.

Notes

  • Rotala wallichii may arrive green when shipped, as colouration depends on lighting, nutrients, and CO₂. With the right care — including iron dosing, high lighting, and CO₂ injection — the plant will quickly develop its signature pink and red tones.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Mayaca Fluviatilis
products.body_html:
Want the look of moss on a stem plant? Mayaca fluviatilis grows fine, needle-like bright green foliage in a dense feathery column — soft enough to read as a moss thicket, but it plants and trims like a stem. It moves visibly with the flow, which is most of its appeal.

What You’ll Receive

Fresh, healthy Mayaca fluviatilis cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®, available in convenient planting formats:

Fresh Cut Plants: Approximately 6+ loose, fresh-cut stems without roots.
Fresh Cut Bunched: Approximately 6+ stems bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy placement.
Fresh Cut Potted: About 6+ stems potted securely in a net pot with rockwool for stability and easy planting.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Mayaca, Bog Moss, Stream Bogmoss
  • Scientific name — Mayaca fluviatilis
  • Origin — South and Central America
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 6–14 in
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Stronger light tightens the internodes and thickens growth
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.0
  • Substrate — Required. Root and water column feeder
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Stem cuttings

Grower’s Notes

  • Soft water is the requirement people miss. Mayaca does noticeably better in soft, slightly acidic water and struggles in hard alkaline tap. If it thins and pales despite good light and dosing, water chemistry is usually the reason.
  • Handle it by the base. The fine foliage strips off where you grip the stem, and those bare nodes do not refoliate.
  • Plant stems a little apart and let them fill in. Packed tight, the inner stems shade out and shed from the bottom.
  • Trim and replant the tops. Bare lower sections are not worth keeping on a plant grown for its texture.
  • The fine leaves trap detritus and suit hair algae. Keep flow moving through the stand and remove affected stems promptly.

Want to go deeper? Read our guide to the Best Background Plants for Your Planted Aquarium.

Notes

  • Live aquatic plants may vary in size, leaf shape, and colouration due to natural growing conditions. Minor melting may occur as the plant adapts to new aquarium parameters — this is normal and temporary under proper care.

products.title: Limnophila Rugosa
products.body_html:
The Limnophila that isn't feathery. Limnophila rugosa breaks with its genus entirely — broad, textured, basil-like leaves in bright green instead of the fine whorled foliage sessiliflora and aromatica are known for. Bushy and dense, and unmistakable next to anything else in a planted tank.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as loose fresh-cut plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approx. 4 loose-cut stems without root
  • Bunched Plants: Approx. 4 stems without root, bundled with foam and a plant weight
  • Potted Plants: Approx. 4 stems without root, potted in rockwool and net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Limnophila Rugosa
  • Scientific name — Limnophila rugosa
  • Also known as — Basil-Leaf Limnophila, Limnophila Butterfly
  • Origin — Tropical Asia
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Broad leaves are the whole point. If your scape already has fine-textured stems, adding another feathery plant just adds bulk. Rugosa's wide crinkled leaves give contrast within the same growth form.
  • Grown emersed it produces a distinct scent from the leaves — the plant is used as a herb in parts of its native range.
  • Trim the tops and replant them; repeated topping builds density.
  • Plant stems an inch apart. Broad leaves shade each other badly when crowded, and the lower leaves drop.
  • Feed at the roots as well as the water column — the large leaves need the input.

products.title: Myriophyllum Mattogrossense Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Myriophyllum mattogrossense is one of the finest-textured background plants available — bright green feathery whorls on slender stems that move with the current. This is the sterile tissue culture version, so the plantlets arrive clean and you separate them yourself.

What You'll Receive

One 4-inch sealed Vitro Culture® bag containing multiple Myriophyllum mattogrossense plantlets, ready to be planted directly in your aquascape.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Mattogrossense Milfoil
  • Scientific name — Myriophyllum mattogrossense
  • Also known as — Myrio, Green Mosaic Plant, Mattogrossense Watermilfoil, Matogrosso milfoil
  • Origin — Mato Grosso, Brazil
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 8-16 inches
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.0
  • Substrate — Nutrient-rich soil helps, but it feeds mainly from the water column
  • Growth habit — Amphibious stem
  • Propagation — Cuttings

Grower's Notes

  • It feeds from the water, not the substrate. Root tabs do little here. Consistent water column dosing — macros and iron — is what keeps the whorls dense and the green bright.
  • Separate the plantlets before planting. Rinse the gel off completely and plant small groups of two or three stems an inch apart. Planted as one lump the centre rots before it roots.
  • Low light makes it leggy, not dead. Under weak lighting the internodes stretch and the feathering thins out. That is a light problem, not a nutrient one.
  • Handle it gently — the foliage is brittle. Fine whorls shed easily when pulled through water or gravel. Use tweezers rather than pushing stems in by hand.
  • Trim on a schedule. At eight to sixteen inches and growing fast, it will overtop anything planted in front of it within weeks. Cut the tops and replant them to keep the group even.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Myriophyllum (Milfoil) Care Guide.

Notes

  • Photos are for reference only. Plant appearance may vary based on lighting and tank conditions. Frequent trimming helps maintain compact growth and fullness.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Bucephalandra Species on Coco Pad [Grower's Choice]
products.body_html:
Attaching Bucephalandra is the slow part — tying rhizomes to wood, waiting months for them to grip. This is that work already done. A mixed Buce planting grown into a natural coconut-shell pad, ready to drop straight into a tank and move around until it looks right.

What You'll Receive

Grower's Choice Bucephalandra species meaning we will randomly pick the species for you. We do not take requests for specific species or colors. Each order is randomly picked with one mystery species. It may be a bit bigger or smaller in size depending on the variety. We do not label or identify the species.

You will get 1 pad with many rhizomes of Bucephalandra. This is a HUGE-SAVING compared to buying an individual rhizome. We do not take requests for specific species or colors. Each piece is randomly picked, with random varieties and a unique shape that approx. 1x2 inches in size. It may be a bit bigger or smaller in size depending on the variety.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Buce, Bucep
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. (Grower's Choice)
  • Also known as — Tribe Schismatoglottideae, family Araceae
  • Origin — Borneo, Indonesia
  • Placement — Foreground to midground; sits on the substrate or on hardscape
  • Mature height — 2-4 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — None needed; the pad sits on top and the rhizomes stay in open water
  • Growth habit — Amphibious epiphyte, feeds from roots and water column
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • Do not bury the pad. Set it on the substrate or wedge it between rocks. Pushing it under gravel buries the rhizomes underneath, and buried Buce rhizomes rot.
  • It is meant to be moved. The whole point of a pad is that you can lift it, reposition it, or take it out for a water change without disturbing anything else. Use that — try it in a few spots before deciding.
  • Expect roughly an inch of growth a year. Bucephalandra is among the slowest plants sold. The pad will look much as it does now for a long time, which is exactly why it works as a permanent feature.
  • Keep the light low. A slow plant under bright light collects algae faster than it grows new leaves. Low to medium light keeps the leaves clean and holds the blues and purples better.
  • The coconut pad will soften over time. That is normal. By the time it does, the rhizomes have knitted together and hold their own shape.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Bucephalandra Care Guide.

products.title: Samolus Valerandi
products.body_html:
Miniature lettuce, underwater. Samolus valerandi forms tight rosettes of rounded, bright green leaves that stack outward from a central crown — a leafy, almost vegetable texture that stands apart from the grasses and stems around it. It grows submerged in an aquarium or emersed in a paludarium or riparium equally well.

What You’ll Receive

Enhance your aquarium with our versatile selection of high-quality aquatic plants, available in three convenient formats:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Includes approximately 1-2 fresh-cut stems without roots. Perfect for flexible planting arrangements.
  • Fresh-Cut Bunched: Approximately 1-2 fresh-cut stems without roots, bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy placement.
  • Fresh-Cut Potted: About 1-2 fresh-cut stems without roots, securely potted in a net pot with rockwool, ensuring stability and healthy growth.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Samolus Valerandi
  • Scientific name — Samolus valerandi
  • Also known as — Samolus parviflorus, Samolus floribundus, Lysimachia parvifolia, Water Mini Lettuce, Water Pimpernel
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 2–6 in
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Strong light keeps the rosettes compact

  • Keep it under 78°F. Samolus sits at the cooler end of the range and loses compactness in a warm tank. It suits room-temperature setups better than a tropical community running at 80°F+.

products.title: Bacopa Platinum Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Almost no green at all. Bacopa monnieri 'Platinum' is the albino form of the toughest stem plant in the hobby — white to palest cream foliage against dark substrate. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format, which matters more here than on most plants: an algae outbreak introduced with the plant is very hard to recover from on foliage this slow and this pale.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as a Tissue Culture package with vitamin liquid/gel
  • Package size: Approx. 4 inches
  • Sustainable growth aquarium plant species
  • Great value! Nice specimen!
  • Tissue Culture Technology | 100% Free from Snail, Algae, Pathogen, and Bacteria plus Extended Shelf Life on all in Vitro Plants

Plant Profile

  • Common name — White Moneywort, White Water Hyssop
  • Scientific name — Bacopa monnieri 'Platinum'
  • Also known as — Bacopa Platinum
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species is pantropical
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Small tissue-cultured plantlets, roughly 1-2 inches
  • Mature height — 6-12 inches
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — Medium to high. Under weak light it stretches thin and pale reaching for more
  • CO₂ — Required. With almost no chlorophyll, it needs every advantage available
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5. Stability matters more than any specific value
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate plus regular water column dosing
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • White tissue cannot photosynthesise. That is the whole difficulty in one sentence. Plain Bacopa monnieri survives neglect because it produces energy efficiently; Platinum produces almost none, so every other condition has to compensate.
  • It can revert to green. Green shoots photosynthesise properly and will outgrow the white growth if left. Cut them out at the base to keep the stand white.
  • Strong light keeps it low and creeping; weak light makes it stretch and thin. Neither is unhealthy, but only one looks like the photographs.
  • Separate the plantlets and plant them an inch apart, and rinse the gel off completely — on a plant this slow, gel-fed algae in the first weeks is hard to reverse.

products.title: Micranthemum Glomeratus (Pearl Weed)
products.body_html:
Want one plant that can be a carpet or a hedge? Pearl Weed does both — trimmed low it creeps sideways into a fine bright-green mat, left alone it grows upright into a bushy column. Few plants change role that completely depending on how you cut them.

You may know it as Micranthemum micranthemoides or Hemianthus micranthemoides. Those are the same plant — see the note below.

What You’ll Receive

Enhance your aquascape with our premium-quality Micranthemum glomeratus, available in three flexible planting formats:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approx. 6+ unrooted, loose fresh-cut stems – flexible for custom layout
  • Fresh-Cut Bunched: Approx. 6+ unrooted stems bundled with foam and plant weight for easy placement
  • Fresh-Cut Potted: Approx. 6+ unrooted stems securely potted in a net pot with rockwool for stable growth

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pearl Weed, also known as Pearl Grass, Baby Tears
  • Scientific name — Micranthemum glomeratus
  • Also known as — Micranthemum micranthemoides, Hemianthus micranthemoides (both outdated)
  • Origin — Florida
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6+ fresh-cut stems, roughly 2-4 in
  • Mature height — 2–4 in trimmed, taller left upright
  • Suits — 5 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Why two scientific names?

Pearl Weed was sold for decades as Micranthemum micranthemoides (also written Hemianthus micranthemoides), and most aquarists still know it by those names.

Micranthemum micranthemoides was a real species from the tidal river margins of the eastern United States. It has not been recorded in the wild since the 1940s and is considered extinct. The plant circulating in the hobby under that label was correctly identified in 2011 as a different, living species — Micranthemum glomeratus, from Florida.

So the plant you receive is Micranthemum glomeratus: the same Pearl Weed you have always bought, correctly named.

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium. More light gives tighter, denser growth
  • CO₂ — Not required. It carpets faster with it, but does not need it
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient substrate makes a visible difference
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed in paludariums
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Trimming decides what plant you get. Cut it back repeatedly and it branches sideways into a carpet. Leave it and it climbs into a soft green bush. Decide which you want before planting, because the two need different spacing.
  • Don't bury the stems deeply. They are fine and rot if pushed too far into substrate — plant just enough to hold them.
  • Replant the trimmings. Cut tops root readily at the nodes, so one portion fills a foreground over a couple of months at no extra cost.
  • In a nano tank its tiny leaves work as a background filler as well as a carpet — unusual flexibility for a single species.

Prefer the sterile format? See Pearl Weed Vitro Culture, free of snails and algae.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Micranthemum Care Guide.

Notes

  • Images shown are sample representations only. Live plants may vary in size, colour, and form based on growing conditions. Unless stated otherwise, plants may arrive in emersed form and are not guaranteed to be pest- or pesticide-free.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Salvinia Minima
products.body_html:
Need nitrate gone and algae starved out fast? Salvinia Minima does it quicker than almost anything. Small quilted leaves with water-repellent hairs spread across the surface, soaking up nutrients and shading the tank below — and it grows fast enough that thinning it becomes a weekly job.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as a small portion
  • Approx. 2" x 2" in size

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Salvinia Minima, Water Spangles
  • Scientific name — Salvinia minima
  • Plant type — Floating fern
  • Placement — Floating on the surface
  • Mature height — 0.5–1 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner. Close to unkillable
  • Light — Medium to high, though it manages on less
  • CO₂ — Not required! It takes carbon straight from the air
  • Water — 65–85°F · pH 6.5–7.5
  • Feeding — Water column
  • Propagation — Runners; it multiplies on its own

Grower’s Notes

  • Thin it every week. This is the fastest-spreading plant we sell, and left alone it forms a solid mat that shades out everything beneath it.
  • The leaf hairs repel water, so it tolerates surface movement far better than Red Root Floater or Frogbit — a good choice if your filter breaks the surface.
  • Yellowing usually means iron or micronutrients. Floating plants feed entirely from the water column and show a deficiency before rooted plants do.
  • Bigger sister plant: if you want the same look at three times the leaf size, see Salvinia Natans.

Notes

  • Cannot ship to Texas. Salvinia minima is listed as an invasive species there — please do not order if you are in Texas.
