products.title: Alternanthera Ficoidea Rainbow
products.body_html:
Read this first: this is not a true aquatic plant. Alternanthera ficoidea 'Rainbow' is a garden and terrarium plant. Kept underwater it holds its red, yellow and green variegation for several months and then needs a spell of emersed growth to recover. Bought with that in mind, few plants carry this much colour.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as loose Fresh-cut Plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Fresh-cut plants | approx. 5 stems, loose fresh-cut plants without root
  • Bunched plants | approx. 5 fresh-cut plants without root bundle with foam, and plant's weight
  • Potted plants | approx. 5 fresh-cut plants potted with net pot and rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Rainbow Alternanthera
  • Scientific name — Alternanthera ficoidea 'Rainbow'
  • Also known as — Rainbow Joseph's Coat
  • True aquatic — No
  • Best suited to — Terrarium, vivarium, riparium, paludarium or bog planting
  • Origin — South America; widely cultivated as a garden plant
  • Placement — Midground
  • Shipped size — Approx. 5 fresh-cut stems, roughly 3-6 inches
  • Mature height — 4-8 inches
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up, or any humid terrarium
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended when submerged
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs; also feeds from the water column
  • Growth habit — Non-aquatic; submerged use is temporary, emersed growth is permanent
  • Propagation — Cuttings

Grower's Notes

  • This is not a true aquatic plant, and we would rather say so. Submerged it survives and even puts on a few inches over several months, but it does not grow indefinitely underwater. Plan to rotate it out to a humid emersed setup to recover, or treat it as a seasonal accent.
  • It is at its best above the waterline. In a riparium, paludarium, vivarium or bog planting with consistently wet soil and high humidity, the red-yellow-green variegation is far stronger and the plant grows without a time limit.
  • Light drives the colour range. Under moderate light the foliage leans green. Strong light — bright LED or partial sun emersed — is what brings out the reds and yellows that give it the name.
  • Take cuttings before it declines. Root fresh tops in wet soil while the parent is still strong. Waiting until the submerged plant fades usually means the cuttings are too weak to take.
  • Want permanent colour underwater? Alternanthera reineckii is the same genus, fully submersible, and stays red indefinitely.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Alternanthera Care Guide.

products.title: Rotala Macrandra
products.body_html:
The plant that separates good tanks from great ones. Rotala macrandra carries the largest leaves in the genus — broad, soft and translucent — in a red that runs from rose to deep crimson. It is also the least forgiving Rotala we sell. Light, CO₂ and iron all have to be right at the same time, and the plant tells you immediately when one of them slips.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as emerged fresh-cut plants without root
  • Fresh-cut plants | approx. 6 loose fresh-cut plants
  • Bunched plants | approx. 6 fresh-cut plants bundle with foam and plant weight
  • Potted plants | approx. 6 fresh-cut plants potted with net pot and rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Rotala Macrandra
  • Scientific name — Rotala macrandra
  • Also known as — Giant Red Rotala, Rotala Rose
  • Origin — India
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — High. Below that the stems stretch, the lower leaves drop and the red fades to a washed bronze
  • CO₂ — Required. This is the one Rotala where injection is not optional in practice
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.0. Soft water gives the best colour
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate plus water column dosing; iron in particular drives the red
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • The leaves are thin enough to be an algae magnet. Soft, broad foliage collects detritus wherever flow is weak, and algae follow within days. Steady circulation through the group matters as much as the lighting does.
  • Lean nitrate is what makes it red. Fed heavily it grows green and leafy no matter how strong the light — hold iron and micros steady while keeping nitrate modest.
  • Trim before it reaches the surface. Once the tops shade the stems beneath, the lower half strips bare and does not recover.
  • Replant the tops and discard the old bases. Cuttings root and colour up faster than the stumps they came from.
  • If this proves too demanding, Rotala macrandra 'Green' has the same soft, round-leaved habit without the pigment demand — no iron chase, no colour to lose.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Rotala Care Guide.

Notes

  • Pictures are not the actual plants you will receive, but a sample representation. Unless specific, we don't guarantee aquatic plants will be free of pests, pesticides, grow emerged, or submerge.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Anubias Golden (Small Size)
products.body_html:
Bright yellow-green leaves in a genus that is otherwise uniformly dark. Anubias Golden pushes new growth in a golden-lime tone that deepens toward green as each leaf matures. This is the young grade — small now, growing into full size in your tank.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as young, miniature size Anubias Golden
  • Sustainable growth Anubias species
  • Fresh and clean, grow direct from our high technology lab farm
  • Young plants grow in a controlled laboratory environment

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Golden Anubias (Small)
  • Scientific name — Anubias barteri 'Golden'
  • Also known as — Anubias Golden Nana
  • Origin — Cultivated variety; the genus is native to West and Central Africa
  • Placement — Midground, attached to hardscape
  • Mature height — 2-4 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Shade suits it; strong light means algae on slow-turning leaves.
  • CO₂ — Not required. Occasional liquid fertiliser deepens the colour.
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Not required. Epiphyte — attach the rhizome to wood or stone and never bury it.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious; also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • The gold is new growth, not variegation. Each leaf emerges pale golden-lime and darkens with age, so the colour sits at the growing tip. That also means it is normally pigmented — no harder to grow than any other Anubias.
  • Place it against something dark. The pale new growth is the whole point and it disappears against light sand or pale stone. Dark wood or black lava rock is where it earns its price.
  • Buy small when you need several. Anubias adds roughly a leaf a month at any size, so a group bought young costs a fraction and catches up within a year.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Roots can go into substrate; the rhizome cannot. Buried, it rots.
  • Lab-grown means no snails, no algae and no pesticide residue — safe for a shrimp tank with no quarantine.

Want the full-size plant? See Anubias Golden Nana.

products.title: Helanthium Quadricostatus (Echinodorus) Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Helanthium quadricostatus is the broad-leaved chain sword — wider blades than the Tenellum forms, spreading by runner into a low green band across the front of a tank. No CO₂, medium light, and it does the work itself once rooted.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as a Tissue Culture package with vitamin liquid/gel
  • Package size: Approx. 4 inches
  • Sustainable growth aquarium plants species
  • Great value! Nice specimen!
  • Tissue Culture Technology | 100% Free from Snail, Algae, Pathogen, and Bacteria plus Extended Shelf Life on all in Vitro Plants

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Broad Leaf Chain Sword
  • Scientific name — Helanthium quadricostatus
  • Also known as — Helanthium bolivianum 'Quadricostatus', Echinodorus quadricostatus, Bolivian Sword Plant
  • Origin — South America
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 4-8 inches
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.5-7.5
  • Substrate — Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs; this is a root feeder
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rosette
  • Propagation — Runners

Grower's Notes

  • Leave the runners attached until the daughter roots. Each runner sets a new rosette a few inches out. Cutting it free early stalls both plants; once it has its own roots it can be lifted and moved anywhere.
  • Broader blades than the other chain swords. If Tenellum has looked too grassy or too fine in your layout, this is the same habit at a heavier leaf — it reads as a plant rather than as turf.
  • Feed the roots, not the water. Chain swords take most of their nutrition from the substrate. Root tabs under the planting area matter far more than liquid dosing.
  • Height depends on light. Under medium light it stays low and spreads. In weak light it stretches taller and thinner reaching for the surface — the plant is fine, it is just growing to a different shape.
  • Thin it once a year. Left alone the rosettes crowd and the middle of the patch goes bare. Pulling every second plant and replanting it keeps the stand even.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Helanthium Chain Sword Care Guide.

products.title: Staurogyne Repens White Albino Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Staurogyne repens is one of the most reliable low carpeting plants in the hobby. The 'White Albino' form takes that familiar shape and strips almost all the green out of it, leaving pale ivory foliage that glows against dark substrate. Less chlorophyll means less energy, so it asks for considerably more than the standard form.

What You'll Receive

One 4-inch sealed Vitro Culture® bag containing healthy Staurogyne Repens 'White Albino' plantlets—ready to rinse, acclimate, and plant with care.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — White Albino Staurogyne
  • Scientific name — Staurogyne repens 'White Albino'
  • Also known as — Staurogyne repens 'Variegated'
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species comes from the Rio Cristalino, Brazil
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Shipped size — Small tissue-cultured plantlets, roughly 1-2 inches
  • Mature height — 2-4 inches
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — Medium. Note the ceiling — strong light bleaches pale tissue
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious creeping stem
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • Pale tissue burns before green tissue does. Do not treat "needs light" as "needs more light". Medium intensity is the target — strong light bleaches the ivory leaves and algae takes hold on them long before it touches anything green in the tank.
  • Reverted green shoots will appear. Any pale sport can throw fully green growth, and green grows faster. Cut those stems out at the base as soon as you spot them or they will take over the group.
  • Feed the substrate. With reduced pigment the plant cannot afford an inefficient root zone. Aquasoil or root tabs under the planting area make the difference between slow and stalled.
  • Plant small portions, spaced out. Rinse the gel off and separate the culture into groups of two or three plantlets an inch apart. Dense clumps shade their own bases, which this plant recovers from poorly.
  • Want the same carpet without the difficulty? Standard Staurogyne repens is a Beginner plant with the same shape and growth habit — the albino form is a collector's plant, not a workhorse.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Staurogyne Repens Care Guide.

Notes

  • Photos shown are sample representations. Actual plant appearance may vary depending on lighting, CO₂, and care. This albino variant is fragile and may melt if not given proper light and nutrients. Not recommended for beginners.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Saururus Cernuus (Lizard's Tail)
products.body_html:
A marginal plant, happiest with its head above water. Saururus cernuus — Lizard's Tail — grows broad heart-shaped leaves on upright arching stems, and it belongs in the wet transitional zone rather than fully submerged: paludariums, ripariums, Wabi-Kusa and shallow margins. Grown emersed it may throw the drooping white flower spike the common name refers to.

What You'll Receive

Available in three convenient planting formats to suit your aquatic or semi-aquatic design:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approx. 3–4 loose, fresh-cut stems without roots
  • Bunched Plants: Approx. 3–4 fresh-cut stems bundled with plant weight for easy placement
  • Potted Plants: Approx. 3–4 fresh-cut stems potted in rockwool within a net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Lizard's Tail
  • Scientific name — Saururus cernuus
  • Also known as — Heartleaf, Swamp Lily, Water Dragon
  • Origin — North America
  • Placement — Paludarium, riparium and marginal zones; midground if submerged
  • Shipped size — Approx. 3–4 stems, usually emersed-grown
  • Mature height — 6–14 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 65–78°F · pH 6.0–7.5, soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — wet soil, nutrient substrate or rockwool
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Strongly prefers emersed or shallow marginal growth
  • Propagation — Stem cuttings, or division of the underground rhizome

Grower's Notes

  • It is a marginal plant, not a submerged one. Saururus grows at the water's edge with its roots wet and its leaves in air. Fully submerged it survives but stays smaller and slower, and the broad heart-shaped leaves that make it worth buying develop best above the waterline. Plan it into a paludarium or riparium rather than a standard tank.
  • Arriving stock is emersed-grown, so a submerged planting will drop its first leaves as it converts. Judge it on the growth that follows.
  • Give it a fed substrate. It roots strongly and feeds through those roots — liquid dosing alone gives thin pale growth.
  • It spreads by underground rhizome as well as by cuttings, so an established clump quietly widens rather than staying in one spot.
  • In an open-top or riparium setup it can flower — a slender white spike that curves over, which is where 'Lizard's Tail' comes from.

Notes

  • Photos shown are sample representations only. Plants may arrive in emersed form and adapt once planted. We do not guarantee plants are free from pests or pesticides unless otherwise specified.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Cryptocoryne Flamingo
products.body_html:
The pink Crypt everyone wants and few keep. Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Pink Flamingo' carries pink and white variegation across the whole leaf — not a tint over green, but a genuine loss of chlorophyll. That is what makes the colour so striking and what makes the plant so slow and so unforgiving. Buy it knowing that.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as small Bare-root Plants or Potted plants
  • Bare-root plant | one small size, loose rooted plants
  • Potted plant | one rooted small size plant, potted with net pot and rockwool
  • Young plants grow in a controlled laboratory environment

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pink Flamingo Crypt
  • Scientific name — Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Pink Flamingo'
  • Also known as — Crypt Flamingo, Cryptocoryne Pink Panther
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species is native to Sri Lanka
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 3–5 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced. The variegation is why
  • Light — Medium to high. It needs more light than a green Crypt to make the same energy
  • CO₂ — Recommended. It holds colour and compact form far better with it
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.5–7.5. Hard water suits it, as it does most Crypts
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Substrate runners

Grower’s Notes

  • Pink means less chlorophyll, which means less margin. A green Crypt survives neglect. Pink Flamingo doesn't — it grows slowly even at its best, so any setback costs months rather than weeks.
  • Expect it to melt after planting and rebuild from the roots over several weeks. That is normal for the genus and slower here than in green forms.
  • Place it once and leave it. Every move triggers another melt, and this plant recovers slowly.
  • Reversion happens. Under weak light or thin feeding it may push greener leaves — the plant compensating for lost pigment.
  • Want the colour with less risk? Cryptocoryne petchii 'Pink' is a beginner plant with a soft pink tone over green rather than true variegation.

Three ways to buy this plant. This listing is the established plant, bare-root or potted — the fastest to look like the photograph. There is also a 4-inch Vitro Culture® bag with several sterile plantlets, and a small Vitro Culture® cup with one small rooted plant — the cheapest way in, and the slowest.

products.title: Java Fern Narrow Mini
products.body_html:
Want Java Fern at its smallest and slimmest? 'Narrow Mini' combines both traits — narrow upright leaves on an ultra-compact plant, giving vertical movement at a scale that suits nano tanks and fine hardscape without swamping it.

products.title: Cryptocoryne Pink Flamingo | Small Vitro Culture Cup
products.body_html:
Rose-pink leaves with fine variegation — the most sought-after Cryptocoryne there is, and one of the most demanding. Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Pink Flamingo' is sold here in the small Vitro Culture® cup, the least expensive way into a plant that is otherwise costly per specimen.

What You'll Receive

One sealed small Vitro Culture® cup (1.7" × 1.7"), lab-grown and free of snails, algae and pesticides.

  • 1 Cup: one cup containing 1 small rooted plant
  • 5 Cups: five cups, each containing 1 small rooted plant

These are young tissue-cultured plants with their roots already formed — small on arrival, and grown on in your tank.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pink Flamingo Crypt
  • Scientific name — Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Pink Flamingo'
  • Also known as — Crypt Flamingo, Cryptocoryne Pink Panther
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species is native to Sri Lanka
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 3-5 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — Medium to high. Strong light intensifies the pink.
  • CO₂ — Recommended. It holds colour and compact form far better with it.
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.5-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs under the crown.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rosette; also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Runners, slowly

Grower's Notes

  • The pink is why it is difficult. Pink leaves carry far less chlorophyll than green ones, so this plant photosynthesises less efficiently than any standard wendtii and has much less margin for poor light, unstable conditions or neglect. Do not assume ordinary Crypt Wendtii's toughness carries over — it does not.
  • One small plant is a starting point, not a display specimen. This is the small-cup format: a young tissue-cultured plant bought cheaply and grown on. Expect a year before it looks like the photograph. If you want an established plant now, buy the loose listing instead.
  • Expect a heavy melt. All crypts shed leaves on a change of conditions, and Pink Flamingo does it harder than most. Leave it alone for three to four weeks and let it rebuild from the roots — pulling it up is what turns a recoverable melt into a loss.
  • Plant the crown at substrate level. Bury the roots and leave the growing point exposed. A buried crown rots from the centre and a slow plant does not recover.
  • New growth often returns greener before the pink comes back. Judge the colour once it has settled, not on the first leaves.

Three ways to buy this plant. This listing is the small cup — one young rooted plant, the cheapest way in and the slowest. There is also a 4-inch Vitro Culture® bag with several plantlets, and an established bare-root or potted plant if you want size straight away.

Notes

Cryptocoryne species may experience "crypt melt" when first introduced to a new aquarium environment. This is a normal adaptation process. With stable water conditions, the plant typically regrows healthy new leaves from its root system.

products.title: Mixed Lotus Seeds – Assorted Colors for Ponds, Water Gardens, and Aquascapes
products.body_html:
Growing a lotus from seed takes about a week to sprout and a season to flower, and the seed itself is the cheapest way into a plant that otherwise ships as an expensive tuber. This is a mixed lot — pink, white, yellow and multi-coloured varieties — so you find out what you have when it blooms.

What You'll Receive

  • Scientific Name: Nelumbo nucifera
  • Common Name: Lotus
  • Product Type: Mixed Lotus Seeds (Hardy and Tropical Varieties)
  • Light Requirement: Full Sun
  • Planting Medium: Heavy clay soil or aquatic planting media
  • Germination Time: 1–7 days after soaking
  • Ideal Use: Outdoor ponds, decorative water gardens, patio water containers

How to Grow Lotus Seeds

  • 1. Scarify the seed. Lotus seeds are oval with one pointed end and one rounded end. Do not file the pointed (embryo) end. Instead, gently file the rounded end until you see the white inner layer. This helps water enter the seed and encourages germination.
  • 2. Soak the seed. Place the scarified seed in a container of warm, clean water (around 75–85°F or 24–29°C). Change the water daily to keep it fresh.
  • 3. Sprouting. Within 1–7 days, the seed will swell and a sprout will emerge. Allow the sprout to grow 4–6 inches before planting.
  • 4. Transfer to soil. Plant the sprouted seed into a pot filled with heavy clay soil or aquatic planting media. Submerge the pot under 2–4 inches of water.
  • 5. Growing in water. Place the potted seedling in a sunny, warm location. As it matures, the lotus will send leaves above the water's surface and eventually produce stunning blooms.

Grower's Notes

  • Filing the wrong end kills the seed. The pointed end holds the embryo. File the rounded end only, and only until the white layer shows — going deeper damages what you are trying to germinate. This one step accounts for most failed lotus seeds.
  • Change the soaking water daily. Stale water fouls and the seed rots before it sprouts. Fresh warm water every day for the first week is the difference between a 1-7 day germination and nothing.
  • Do not plant the sprout too early. Wait until the shoot is four to six inches long. Planted shorter, it struggles to reach light through the water and stalls.
  • Lotus needs more sun than a water lily. Full sun all day is the target. In partial sun you will get leaves and no flowers, and lotus leaves are large enough to be worth growing on their own — but flowering needs the light.
  • Expect flowers in the second season. A seed-grown lotus spends its first year building a rhizome. That is normal and not a sign anything is wrong.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Guide on How to Grow Lotus Flowers from Seeds.

Notes

  • While our lotus seeds (Nelumbo nucifera) are selected for very high sprouting rates, we do not guarantee the flower color or that every seed will successfully grow. Flower coloration may vary naturally. Proper care, growing conditions, and patience are essential for best results.

products.title: Nymphaea Tropical Blue
products.body_html:
Blue flowers for a warm pond. Nymphaea Tropical Blue is a tropical water lily supplied for its clear blue blooms, held above the water on upright stems in the way tropicals do. It wants sun and warmth, and it will not survive a frozen pond — the tuber comes out before frost.

What You'll Receive

  • You will get 1 water lily tuber of Nymphaea Tropical Blue. (organic sprouts tuber)
  • All of our water lilies tubers/rhizomes have been inspected before ship out and guaranteed they are viable and perfect to grow in a proper pond environment. The picture is not the actual product you will receive, but a sample representation.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Tropical Blue Water Lily
  • Scientific name — Nymphaea sp., tropical blue form
  • Type — Tropical water lily
  • Flower — Blue
  • Plant form — Tuber
  • Placement — Ponds and water gardens; centrepiece

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Sunlight — Full sun to partial shade; direct sun for good flowering
  • Water — Warm. Tropical lilies need genuine heat to perform
  • Substrate — Gravel, clay, sand or heavy garden soil in a submerged container
  • Planting angle — Tropical tuber: straight up at 90°, crown level with the soil
  • Feeding — Aquatic fertiliser tablets through the growing season
  • Overwintering — Tropical. Lift the tuber before frost and store it moist and frost-free, or keep it in the pond in warm climates
  • Propagation — Tuber division

Grower's Notes

  • Blue only exists among the tropicals. There is no such thing as a hardy blue water lily — the genes are not in the hardy side of the genus. If blue is what you want, a tropical and its autumn lift are the price of it.
  • Tropical blooms are held above the water on stems rather than floating flat, which makes the colour visible from across a pond.
  • Warmth matters more than for a hardy lily. In a cool pond it does very little until the water climbs into the seventies.
  • Lift the tuber before the first frost and store it moist and frost-free, or treat it as an annual. A tropical left in an icing pond is lost.
  • The pads shade the water, which limits algae and gives fish cover through summer.

New to planting water lilies? Read our complete Water Lily Planting Guide — tuber angle, soil, depth and the one mistake that kills most first lilies.

Notes

  • We don't ship dormant roots. Your tuber arrives fresh and actively growing with 1–2 young leaves already emerged — visible proof it's viable before it leaves us. Young pads may start fully submerged and will reach the surface within about a week in good light.
  • Never release aquatic plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Nymphaea August Koch | Violet-Blue Tropical Water Lily
products.body_html:
A 1922 introduction that propagates itself. Nymphaea 'August Koch' carries large, fragrant violet-blue flowers over olive-green pads, and it is highly viviparous — new plantlets form on the leaves, so one plant becomes several. It was raised at Garfield Park in Chicago and named for August Koch, who bred it alongside George H. Pring.

What You'll Receive

  • You will get 1 young and freshly harvested water lily tuber
  • All of our water lilies tubers/rhizomes have been inspected before ship out and guaranteed they are viable and perfect to grow in a proper pond environment

Plant Profile

  • Common name — August Koch Water Lily
  • Scientific name — Nymphaea 'August Koch'
  • Origin — Garfield Park, Chicago, 1922; bred by August Koch and George H. Pring
  • Parentage — Likely 'Blue Beauty' × 'Mrs. Woodrow Wilson'
  • Type — Tropical water lily, viviparous
  • Flower — Large violet-blue, fragrant
  • Foliage — Olive-green pads
  • Placement — Ponds and containers with still water

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Sunlight — Full sun; at least 6 hours of direct sun daily
  • Water — 70–80°F
  • Substrate — Heavy clay or loam in a submerged container
  • Planting angle — Tropical tuber: straight up at 90°, crown level with the soil
  • Feeding — Water lily fertiliser tablets pushed into the soil every few weeks through the growing season
  • Overwintering — Tropical. In cool climates lift the plant and store the rhizome in damp sand and peat moss at 50–55°F
  • Propagation — Viviparous plantlets on the leaves; also tuber division

Grower's Notes

  • Highly viviparous, which is the practical reason to choose it. Plantlets form on mature pads and can be lifted and potted once they have roots and a leaf of their own. Most lilies only increase by division — this one multiplies through the season on its own.
  • Over a century in cultivation. A 1922 cultivar that is still sold has earned its place on performance, not novelty.
  • Fragrant as well as blue. Scent is not a given among the blue tropicals, so site it where people sit.
  • Wants still water and real warmth — 70–80°F suits it. Keep the pot clear of fountains and waterfall outflows.
  • Leave old pads in place while plantlets are forming. Tidying them away removes the next generation.

New to planting water lilies? Read our complete Water Lily Planting Guide — tuber angle, soil, depth and the one mistake that kills most first lilies.

Notes

  • We don't ship dormant roots. Your tuber arrives fresh and actively growing with 1–2 young leaves already emerged — visible proof it's viable before it leaves us. Young pads may start fully submerged and will reach the surface within about a week in good light.
  • Remove dead leaves and spent flowers to keep the water clean — though leave any pad carrying plantlets until they are ready to lift.
  • Never release aquatic plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Nymphaea King of Siam | Blue Tropical Water Lily
products.body_html:
Nymphaea 'King of Siam' carries double deep purple-blue petals stacked into a full, layered bloom — a 1998 Thai hybrid of 'Larp Prasert' × 'Colorata' by Chaiyaphon Thamasuwan. It is a tropical lily, so it wants heat and sun and comes indoors for winter in a cold climate.

What You'll Receive

  • Shipped bare-root as a tuber, ready to plant on arrival

Plant Profile

  • Common name — King of Siam Blue Tropical Water Lily
  • Scientific name — Nymphaea 'King of Siam'
  • Also known as — Nymphaea 'King of the Blues', Nymphaea 'Chalong Kwan'
  • Type — Tropical, day-blooming; hybrid of 'Larp Prasert' × 'Colorata' (Chaiyaphon Thamasuwan, 1998)
  • Flower — Double deep purple-blue petals
  • Placement — Centrepiece in a pond or water garden
  • Mature height — 12-24 inches
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Sunlight — Full sun, at least 6 hours daily
  • Planting depth — 6-18 inches of water over the tuber
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5; still to slightly moving
  • Soil — Heavy clay or loam, capped with gravel; this is a root feeder
  • Feeding — Water lily fertiliser tablets through the growing season
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • Tropical, not hardy — this decides your winter. The tuber must be lifted and stored in moist conditions over winter unless you are in a warm climate. If you cannot do that, buy a hardy lily instead; they stay in the pond and return on their own.
  • True blue-purple is rare in lilies. Most pond lilies run pink, red, white or yellow. The blue-purple line traces back to N. colorata, which is this plant's parent — that is where the colour comes from.
  • Warm water matters as much as sun. A shaded or spring-fed pond that stays cool will give you pads and very few flowers no matter how much fertiliser goes in.
  • Plant the tuber upright with the crown exposed. Set it in the centre of the pot with the growing point above the soil line, then cap with gravel. Buried crowns rot.
  • Plant at final depth — submerged pads are normal. The young pads may sit completely underwater at first, and they do not need to reach the surface on day one. Given enough sunlight the leaf stems extend on their own and the pads surface within about a week.

New to planting water lilies? Read our complete Water Lily Planting Guide — tuber angle, soil, depth and the one mistake that kills most first lilies.

Notes

  • All water lilies are shipped bare-root (as tubers) and should be planted immediately upon arrival for best results. Bloom and leaf color, size, and shape may vary slightly depending on lighting, water quality, and plant maturity.

products.title: Nymphaea Dang Mameaw | Deep Pink Tropical Water Lily
products.body_html:
The deeper-coloured Mameaw. Nymphaea 'Dang Mameaw', also known as Dang Ma Miew Water Lily, is a day-blooming tropical carrying fragrant deep pink to raspberry-red flowers 4 to 8 inches across, held well above the water. Dang means red in Thai, and that is what separates it from its close relative.

products.title: Ludwigia Senegalensis
products.body_html:
Veins you can actually see. Ludwigia senegalensis runs a network of dark red veins across brick-red to orange leaves, so the pattern reads as detail rather than a flat block of colour — closer to a patterned houseplant than to the usual red stem plant. It is the most distinctive Ludwigia we carry, and the most demanding.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as loose Fresh-cut plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Fresh-cut plants | Approx. 6 stems, loose fresh-cut stems without root
  • Bunched plants | Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems without root, bundled with foam, and lead weight
  • Potted plants | Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems without root, potted with net pot and rockwool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Ludwigia Senegalensis
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia senegalensis
  • Also known as — Ludwigia sp. 'Guinea', Guinea Ludwigia
  • Origin — West Africa
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — Medium to high. The vein pattern and brick-red colour both depend on it
  • CO₂ — Recommended. In practice this plant rarely performs without it
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate plus water column dosing
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim side shoots and replant

Grower's Notes

  • Stability is the requirement, not any single value. Senegalensis punishes swings in CO₂, temperature and dosing more than it punishes any particular parameter being slightly off. A settled, mature tank suits it; a new one usually does not.
  • It throws multiple side shoots readily, so a few stems become a bush faster than most Ludwigia. Trim shoots off to propagate, or leave them for a dense red-orange mass.
  • The veining is what you are paying for, and it needs light to show. Under weak lighting the leaves stay plain green and the pattern disappears.
  • Plant stems separately with space between them. Crowded, the lower leaves shade out and the pattern is lost exactly where you would see it.
  • Frequently confused with Ludwigia glandulosa. They look similar but come from opposite sides of the Atlantic — glandulosa is North American, this is West African.

products.title: Mini Pellia / Mini Coral Moss
products.body_html:
Want texture nothing else in the hobby can give you? Mini Pellia grows in finely branched, deep green fronds that look like miniature coral — dense compact cushions rather than the loose strands of a true moss. It is a liverwort, and it is the detail plant serious aquascapers reach for.

What You’ll Receive

  • Loose Portion: Approximately 2" × 2"
  • Ready to Attach: Suitable for rocks, driftwood, mesh, or other aquarium décor

Portion size and density may vary slightly because this is a natural live plant.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Mini Pellia, Mini Coral Moss, Mini Liverwort
  • Scientific name — Riccardia chamedryfolia
  • Plant type — Liverwort, not a true moss
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, on wood, stone or mesh
  • Mature height — 1–2 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate. Not hard, but slow and unforgiving of neglect
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required, but it rewards CO₂ more than most mosses do
  • Water — Cooler is better; it thrives below about 75°F and struggles in warm tanks
  • Feeding — Water column
  • Propagation — Fragmentation; reattach healthy clippings

Grower’s Notes

  • Temperature is the deciding factor. Riccardia is a cool-water plant — in a tank running above 78°F it thins, browns and slowly gives up no matter how good the light and CO₂ are.
  • Flow matters more than light. The dense fronds trap detritus in still water and rot from the inside, so give it gentle, steady circulation.
  • Tie it on thin and flat. A thick clump smothers itself long before the surface fills in, and this plant is far too slow to recover from that.
  • It attaches slowly. Expect a couple of months before it grips hardscape properly — keep the thread or mesh on until it does.
  • Not to be confused with plain Pellia (Monosolenium tenerum), which is thicker, faster, more brittle and far more heat tolerant.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Aquarium Moss Care Guide.

Notes

  • Photos are for reference. Portion size, density and colour vary naturally. Live plants may carry algae or small hitchhikers — rinsing before adding to your aquarium is recommended.

products.title: Limnophila Aromatica
products.body_html:
Limnophila aromatica is the same rice paddy herb sold in Vietnamese markets, grown underwater. Whorls of narrow leaves sit green on top and purple underneath, and the purple deepens as light intensity climbs. It grows fast enough to fill a background in weeks.

What You'll Receive

Enhance your aquarium with our versatile selection of high-quality aquatic plants, available in three convenient formats:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Includes approximately 6 loose, fresh-cut stems without roots. Perfect for flexible planting arrangements.
  • Fresh-Cut Bunched: Approximately 6 fresh-cut stems without roots, bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy placement.
  • Fresh-Cut Potted: About 6 fresh-cut stems without roots, securely potted in a net pot with rockwool, ensuring stability and healthy growth.

Choose the format that best suits your aquascaping needs and create a vibrant, lush underwater environment with our premium aquatic plants.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Rice Paddy Herb
  • Scientific name — Limnophila aromatica
  • Also known as — Ambulia, ngò om, Vietnamese coriander of the rice fields
  • Origin — Southeast Asia
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 8-16 inches
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs, plus water column dosing
  • Growth habit — Amphibious stem, feeds from roots and water column
  • Propagation — Cuttings

Grower's Notes

  • The purple lives on the underside of the leaf. Viewed from above the plant reads green; from the front, the whorls show violet. Planting it where you look across it rather than down at it is what shows the colour off.
  • The scent comes out of water, not in it. Emersed leaves smell strongly of citrus and cumin when crushed — it is a culinary herb in Vietnam. Submersed growth has little scent, so buy it for the colour and the texture.
  • Trim aggressively and it branches. Cutting the top third repeatedly turns a single stem into a dense bush. Left alone it grows straight to the surface and drops its lower leaves.
  • Iron and light together drive the colour. Medium light with steady micronutrient dosing produces the purple. Strong light without iron gives you a fast green plant instead.
  • Plant stems apart, not in a bundle. Six stems pushed in as one clump shade each other and rot at the base. Space them half an inch apart and let them fill in.

products.title: Vallisneria Nana
products.body_html:
Want the flowing Vallisneria look without a curtain that swallows your tank? Vallisneria nana has the thinnest leaf blade in the genus — roughly 1 mm wide. Fine dark green ribbons that move constantly with the flow, reading as texture rather than as a solid wall.

What You’ll Receive

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approximately 2–3 individual loose, bare-root plants
  • Bunched Plants: Approximately 2–3 individual bare-root plants bundled with foam and a plant weight
  • Potted Plants: Approximately 2–3 individual bare-root plants potted in rockwool and net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Vallisneria Nana, also known as Narrow Leaf Eelgrass
  • Scientific name — Vallisneria nana
  • Also known as — Vallisneria gracilis
  • Origin — Australia
  • Placement — Background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 2-3 bare-root plants, roughly 6-12 in
  • Mature height — 20–30 in, longer in the wild
  • Leaf width — Approx. 1 mm — the narrowest Vallisneria
  • Suits — 20 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium is enough
  • CO₂ — Not required! One of the best background plants for a low-tech tank
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.5–8.0. Handles hard alkaline water better than most
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — root tabs are what drive the runners
  • Growth habit — Fully aquatic
  • Propagation — Substrate runners

Grower’s Notes

  • A 1 mm blade changes how it reads. Jungle Val and Gigantea form solid green curtains. Nana at this width lets light and sightlines through, so you get movement and depth without blocking the back of the tank.
  • Plant the crown at the substrate line, never below it. A buried crown rots, and that is the usual reason a new Val fails in its first fortnight.
  • Don't trim the tops to control height. Cut Vallisneria leaves brown at the cut and stay that way — remove whole leaves at the base instead.
  • It feeds at the roots. In inert gravel it survives but barely spreads; root tabs are what turn three plants into a stand.
  • Still a tall plant at 20–30 inches, and longer in the wild. In a shallow tank it reaches the surface and trails along it.

Want the patterned version? See Vallisneria nana 'Striped', the same narrow blade with brown tiger striping.

products.title: Eleocharis Vivipara
products.body_html:
Hairgrass that goes up, not sideways. Eleocharis vivipara — Giant Hairgrass — grows long slender blades that sway in the current instead of carpeting the floor, and it propagates in an unusual way: baby plants form at the leaf tips rather than on runners. That's what vivipara means, and it's why this Eleocharis behaves nothing like the carpeting species.

What You’ll Receive

  • Bare-root plants | loose, bare-root portion
  • This type of Hairgrass will grow tall, perfect for background aquarium

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Vivipara Hairgrass
  • Scientific name — Eleocharis vivipara
  • Also known as — Giant Hairgrass, Tall Hairgrass, Umbrella Hairgrass
  • Origin — Southeastern United States
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Loose bare-root portion, shorter than mature height
  • Mature height — 6–12 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Daughter plantlets at the leaf tips; also splits at the base

Grower’s Notes

  • Don't buy this one for a carpet. Dwarf Hairgrass and Eleocharis mini spread by runners along the substrate. Vivipara grows upward and multiplies from its own leaf tips — you get a tall grassy stand, not a lawn.
  • Harvest the tip plantlets. Cut them off once they have a few blades and roots, and plant them; that's how one portion becomes a stand.
  • Feed at the roots. It draws most of its nutrition from the substrate, so root tabs matter more than liquid dosing.
  • Trim the tops if it reaches too high — cut blades keep growing from the base.
  • Separate the portion into small clumps before planting rather than sinking it as one mass; the clumps root faster.

products.title: Alternanthera Ficoidea 'Pink'
products.body_html:
Read this first: this is not a true aquatic plant. Alternanthera ficoidea 'Pink' is a terrarium, vivarium and bog plant with vivid pink foliage. It will live submerged in an aquarium for several months — often rooting and gaining height — but it needs a spell growing above water afterwards to recover. Sold on that understanding.

  • Common name — Pink Terrarium Alternanthera
  • Scientific name — Alternanthera ficoidea 'Pink'
  • True aquatic — No
  • Best suited to — Terrarium, vivarium, riparium, pond margin or houseplant in high humidity

products.title: Dwarf Hairgrass Mini | Bulk Pack
products.body_html:
Carpeting is a numbers game. Eleocharis sp. 'Mini' spreads by runners, but the fastest route to a finished carpet is planting many small clumps close together rather than waiting for a few to fill the gaps. This bulk pack gives you 10, 20 or 30 clumps at volume pricing — the practical way to carpet a large foreground in one go.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Dwarf Hairgrass Mini, Mini Hairgrass, Japanese Hairgrass
  • Scientific name — Eleocharis sp. 'Mini'
  • Also known as — Eleocharis acicularis 'Mini', Eleocharis sp. Belem
  • Origin — Cultivated dwarf form
  • Placement — Foreground
  • Shipped size — 10 to 30 clumps, each approx. 1" x 1"

  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5

  • Split every clump before planting. A 1" x 1" clump divides into six or eight small tufts. Planted half an inch apart, those tufts close ranks far faster than the intact clump would spread — so the bulk pack effectively covers several times its own area.

Dwarf Hairgrass Mini is commonly grown emersed and may experience a normal transition period as it adapts to submerged aquarium conditions.

products.title: Subwassertang Moss (Round Pellia)
products.body_html:
Want the look of moss without the maintenance? Subwassertang forms soft, translucent ruffled fronds that tangle into loose bushy clusters — and despite the name, it isn't a moss at all. It's the gametophyte stage of a fern, which is why it behaves so differently from anything else in the tank.

What You’ll Receive

  • Loose Portion: Includes a small, loose portion of Subwassertang Moss (approx. 2" x 2")
  • Ready to Use: Can be attached directly to your aquascaping elements with glue, thread, or simply tucked into crevices

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Subwassertang, Round Pellia, Loma Fern
  • Scientific name — Lomariopsis lineata
  • Plant type — Fern gametophyte (prothallus), not a true moss
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, attached or floating
  • Mature height — 1–2 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner. Tolerates a wide range of conditions
  • Light — Low to medium. It genuinely prefers shade
  • CO₂ — Not required! Denser with it, perfectly happy without
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Feeding — Water column
  • Propagation — Fragmentation; every piece grows on

Grower’s Notes

  • It has no roots and no rhizoids that grip properly. Unlike Java Moss it won't fasten itself to wood quickly — tuck it into crevices, tie it under mesh, or glue it, and give it months to settle.
  • It also works floating. A loose ball drifting at the surface is a legitimate way to keep it, and shrimp will graze it constantly either way.
  • Keep it out of strong flow. The fronds are light and unanchored, so a powerful outflow will simply relocate your Subwassertang to the far end of the tank.
  • It resists algae unusually well for a slow plant, which is why it holds up in long-term scapes where mosses eventually need stripping out.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Aquarium Moss Care Guide.

Notes

  • Photos are for reference. Portion size, density and frond shape vary naturally.

products.title: Hydrocotyle ranunculoides ‘Variegated’
products.body_html:
A floating pennywort with white-edged leaves. Hydrocotyle ranunculoides 'Variegated' grows round scalloped leaves in bright green with creamy-white margins, carried on creeping stems that float across the surface or root along a shallow margin. It is a pond, tub and open-top plant rather than a submerged aquarium one.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as Fresh-cut Plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Fresh Cut plants | approx. 4 stems, loose fresh-cut plants
  • Bunched plants | approx. 4 fresh-cut plants with foam, and plant weight
  • Potted plants | approx. 4 fresh-cut plants with net pot and rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Variegated Floating Pennywort
  • Scientific name — Hydrocotyle ranunculoides 'Variegated'
  • Also known as — Marble Floating Pennywort
  • Origin — North America
  • Placement — Floating, or rooted at a shallow margin
  • Shipped size — Approx. 4 fresh-cut stems
  • Mature height — Around 6 in above the waterline
  • Suits — Ponds, tubs, container gardens and open-top tanks
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Part shade to full sun. Strong light holds the white variegation
  • CO₂ — Not required. Its leaves sit above water, where CO₂ does nothing
  • Water — Hardy in USDA zones 5–11. Shallow water up to 4 in, or wet soil
  • Substrate — Optional. Roots at the nodes wherever it touches damp ground
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Floats or creeps; leaves held above the surface
  • Propagation — Runners — every node roots

Grower’s Notes

  • This is a pond plant, not a submerged aquarium plant. The leaves are held above the waterline on emergent stalks. In a closed aquarium with a lid it will grow but stay poor; in a pond, tub, riparium or open-top tank it does what it is meant to.
  • It spreads fast, so contain it. Every node roots, and in a pond it will cross the surface within a season. Grow it in a basket or planter if you want it to stay where you put it.
  • Strong light keeps the cream margins bright. In shade the variegation fades toward plain green.
  • It is hardy well below freezing at the root, so in most of the US it overwinters outdoors and returns in spring.
  • For a genuinely submersible pennywort, see Hydrocotyle tripartita — smaller three-lobed leaves that grow fully underwater.

Notes

  • Hydrocotyle ranunculoides 'Variegated' is a vigorous grower; manage responsibly to prevent spreading.
  • Never release aquarium or pond plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Rotala Orange Juice Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Rotala Orange Juice (Rotala rotundifolia 'Orange Juice') Vitro Culture®

Rotala Orange Juice, a vibrant form of Rotala rotundifolia, is celebrated for its refreshing orange-peach coloration and easy adaptability in aquascaped tanks. With narrow, soft leaves that turn rich shades of orange to red color under strong lighting and CO₂, this stem plant is a favorite for aquascapers looking to create bold contrast and dynamic texture in midground or background zones.

This Vitro Culture® version is grown in a 4-inch sealed bag, offering robust, healthy plantlets propagated in a sterile environment. Free from algae, snails, and contaminants, it’s ideal for shrimp tanks and precision aquascaping projects.

🌿 Key Features:

  • Scientific Name: Rotala rotundifolia 'Orange Juice'

  • Common Name: Rotala Orange Juice, Rotala OJ

  • Growth Form: Upright stem plant with rounded, slightly soft leaves

  • Coloration: Orange to Red

  • Light Demand: Medium to high

  • Growth Rate: Moderate to fast

🧪 Vitro Culture® Advantages:

🎨 Aquascaping Benefits:

  • Easy to trim and propagate for lush groupings or vertical layering

  • Blends beautifully with red and green plant varieties

🌱 Propagation & Growth:

  • Propagation Method: Cut top shoots or side stems and replant

products.title: Rotala Wallichii Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Rotala wallichii is a beautiful stem plant that grows in South-East Asian waters that are soft and slightly acidic. It blooms with flowers that are bright purple. Even though it's not easy to grow, this plant is very popular.

Rotala wallichii was a stem plant with small, finely-toothed, reddish-pink to pink leaves. It looks best when there are a lot of stems in a group. It can also be used in the foreground and in smaller tanks if it is cut at the right time. Adding CO2 to the air helps plants grow a lot. It likes water that is soft and a bit acidic.

products.title: Staurogyne Repens | Bulk Pack
products.body_html:
Carpeting a whole foreground one portion at a time is slow and expensive. Staurogyne repens spreads by creeping sideways rather than by runner, so the fastest route to a finished carpet is planting enough stems at the start — which is what this pack is for.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Staurogyne Repens cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®, sold as loose fresh-cut stems in bulk pack sizes:

  • 10 Pack: Includes 10 portions, with approximately 6 loose fresh-cut stems per portion. Total approximately 60 stems.
  • 20 Pack: Includes 20 portions, with approximately 6 loose fresh-cut stems per portion. Total approximately 120 stems.
  • 30 Pack: Includes 30 portions, with approximately 6 loose fresh-cut stems per portion. Total approximately 180 stems.

Stems may arrive with some roots or without roots depending on growth stage and harvest condition. Each portion is freshly cut and prepared for planting in freshwater aquariums.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Staurogyne Repens, Creeping Staurogyne
  • Scientific name — Staurogyne repens
  • Origin — Rio Cristalino, Brazil
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Shipped size — 60 to 180 fresh-cut stems, roughly 2-4 in each
  • Mature height — 2-4 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium. More light means tighter, denser growth
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root and water column feeder
  • Growth habit — Amphibious creeping stem
  • Propagation — Cuttings — replant trimmed tops straight into the substrate

Grower's Notes

  • Buy enough to plant it properly. Staurogyne creeps rather than running, so it fills gaps slowly. Sixty stems planted two inches apart cover roughly a 12x12 inch area on day one — far faster than waiting for six stems to spread across it.
  • Plant the stems a couple of inches apart and let them creep together. Packed tight from day one, the inner stems shade each other and drop their lower leaves.
  • Trim the tops early rather than waiting for height. Every cut forces side shoots, and that branching is what turns a row of stems into an actual carpet.
  • Replant every trimming — cut tops root readily, so the carpet keeps expanding at no extra cost.
  • Yellowing lower leaves usually means light isn't reaching the base, either because the mat has thickened or a taller plant is shading it.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Staurogyne Repens Care Guide.

Notes

  • Pictures are not the actual plants you will receive, but a sample representation. Unless specified, we do not guarantee aquatic plants will be free of pests, snails, algae, or pesticides. Plants may be grown emersed or submerged. Some melting, leaf loss, or transition is normal as plants adapt to a new aquarium environment.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

featured_image.alt: Staurogyne repens is a top pick for aquarium enthusiasts who love planted tanks. It's especially popular as a go-to foreground carpet plant. This plant comes from South America and belongs to the Acanthaceae family. What's so special about it? Well, it grows in a neat way, has a striking green color, and is great at making your tank floor look like a luxurious carpet in aquascapes. It's like nature's art installation right in your aquarium.

products.title: Bucephalandra Theia
products.body_html:
Theia runs warm — golden to copper-bronze with a soft iridescence, on narrow, gently curved leaves. It is one of the few Bucephalandra that reads gold rather than blue, green or red, which makes it useful where the rest of a scape is cool-toned.

What You'll Receive

Sold as loose Bare-Root or Potted plants:

  • 1 Bare-Root: Approximately 5+ leaves
  • 5 Bare-Root: Approximately 25+ leaves total
  • 10 Bare-Root: Approximately 50+ leaves total
  • 1 Potted: Approximately 10+ leaves
  • 5 Potted: Approximately 50+ leaves total
  • 10 Potted: Approximately 100+ leaves total

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Theia Buce
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. 'Theia'
  • Also known as — Buce Theia
  • Origin — Borneo (genus range)
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, attached to hardscape
  • Mature height — 2-4 inches
  • Growth rate — Very slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Stronger light lifts the gold and copper, but brings algae the plant is too slow to outgrow.
  • CO₂ — Not required. Speeds growth and enriches colour if you already run it.
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — None needed. Epiphyte; feeds from the water column.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rhizome creeper; grows submersed or emersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • Gold is the gap in most Buce collections. The genus runs heavily to blue, green, purple and red. A warm copper-gold sits against all of them, which is why Theia is worth having even if you already keep several varieties.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie or glue it to wood or rock and leave it exposed; buried rhizomes rot.
  • Farm-raised, not wild-collected. All the Bucephalandra we carry is farm-grown, and much of it is raised from tissue culture rather than collected from Borneo.
  • At under two inches of growth a year, coverage has to be bought rather than waited for. Start with more plants if you want a filled-in look.
  • Some leaf melt after shipping is normal. The rhizome survives and pushes new submersed leaves within a few weeks.

Not to be confused with Bucephalandra Theia Green, which is a separate variety.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Bucephalandra Care Guide.

Notes

Like most Bucephalandra, minor leaf melt may occur after introduction as the plant adjusts to new water parameters. This is normal and temporary — new submersed leaves regrow from the rhizome once the plant stabilizes.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Bucephalandra Pink Malawi
products.body_html:
Looking for pink in a plant that isn't fussy? Bucephalandra 'Pink Malawi' carries a soft rose-to-bronze iridescence that shifts under the light — pink, copper, a hint of violet — on a compact plant that asks for nothing but low light and a piece of wood to sit on.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as loose Bare-Root or Potted plants:

  • 1 Bare-Root: Approximately 6+ leaves
  • 5 Bare-Root: Approximately 25+ leaves total
  • 10 Bare-Root: Approximately 50+ leaves total
  • 1 Potted: Approximately 6+ leaves
  • 5 Potted: Approximately 25+ leaves total
  • 10 Potted: Approximately 50+ leaves total

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pink Malawi Buce
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. 'Pink Malawi'
  • Origin — Borneo, Indonesia
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, on wood or stone
  • Mature height — 2–4 in
  • Growth rate — Very slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner. Rare to find, easy to keep
  • Light — Low to medium; stronger light draws out the pink and bronze
  • CO₂ — Not required. It deepens colour and speeds growth, nothing more
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Feeding — Root and water column
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower’s Notes

  • Never bury the rhizome. Roots may sit in substrate; the rhizome cannot. Buried, it rots — the usual way a good Buce is lost.
  • The pink is a lighting response and RGB lighting shows it best. Under warm white light the same plant reads bronze or plain green, which is why photos vary so much between sellers.
  • Expect it green on arrival. Colour builds over weeks to months of submersed growth — judge it at three months, not on day one.
  • Farm-raised, not wild-collected. All the Bucephalandra we carry is farm-grown, and much of it is raised from tissue culture rather than collected from Borneo.
  • Minor leaf melt after introduction is normal. New submersed leaves regrow from the rhizome once it settles.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Bucephalandra Care Guide.

Notes

  • Photos are for reference; colour intensity and leaf size vary with lighting and tank conditions.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Ludwigia Arcuata Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
The finest-leaved Ludwigia. Ludwigia arcuata grows narrow needle-like leaves on slender arching stems — a texture closer to a Rotala than to the broad-leaved Ludwigia most tanks have — and it runs from bright green through orange to deep red as light increases. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® (tissue culture) format.

What You'll Receive

  • One (1) Vitro Culture® 4-Inch Bag of Ludwigia arcuata
  • Yield: Many small healthy stems for planting across your aquascape

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Narrow Leaf Ludwigia
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia arcuata
  • Also known as — Narrow Leaf Repens (a trade name; it is not a form of Ludwigia repens)
  • Origin — Southeastern United States
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — 4-inch bag of small unrooted stems
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium to fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. High light is what produces the deep red
  • CO₂ — Recommended for best colour and compact growth
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Not required. It feeds well from the water column with liquid dosing
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • It is not a narrow-leaved Ludwigia repens. The trade name says otherwise, but arcuata is a separate species with genuinely needle-fine leaves. If you already own repens and want more of the same, this will look quite different beside it — which is usually the point.
  • It works in inert gravel. Unlike most red stems, arcuata takes what it needs from the water column, so consistent liquid dosing matters more than a fed substrate. Useful if you are not running aquasoil.
  • Rinse the gel off and separate the stems before planting, spacing them an inch apart. Planted as a clump the fine foliage shades itself and the lower stems rot.
  • Trim and replant the tops. Cuttings colour faster than the stumps regrow.
  • The needle-fine texture reads best against broad-leaved plants and mosses — that contrast is most of the effect.

Notes

  • Images are for reference only. Actual plant appearance may vary based on lighting and aquarium conditions. Please follow proper acclimation steps when introducing tissue culture plants to your aquarium.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Nymphaea Director George T. Moore | Violet-Purple Tropical Water Lily
products.body_html:
Deep violet-purple, and it blooms until frost. Nymphaea 'Director George T. Moore' is a tropical water lily carrying large star-shaped flowers 4–6 inches across in a strong violet-purple, strongly fragrant, over broad rounded green pads. It flowers profusely from June until the first frost stops it.

What You'll Receive

  • You will get 1 young and freshly harvested water lily tuber
  • All of our water lilies tubers/rhizomes have been inspected before ship out and guaranteed they are viable and perfect to grow in a proper pond environment

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Director George T. Moore Water Lily
  • Scientific name — Nymphaea 'Director George T. Moore'
  • Type — Tropical water lily, day-blooming
  • Flower — Violet-purple, star-shaped, 4–6 inches across, highly fragrant
  • Foliage — Broad, rounded green pads
  • Bloom season — June to frost; profuse
  • Placement — Ponds and water gardens; centrepiece

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Sunlight — Full sun; at least 6 hours of direct sun for good flowering
  • Water depth — 12 to 24 inches, in still or slow-moving water
  • Substrate — Heavy clay or loam in a submerged container, which also makes seasonal lifting easier
  • Planting angle — Tropical tuber: straight up at 90°, crown level with the soil
  • Feeding — Aquatic fertiliser tablets through the growing season
  • Overwintering — Tropical. Treat as an annual, or lift and store the tuber (see Grower's Notes)
  • Propagation — Tuber division

Grower's Notes

  • How to store the tuber over winter. After the first frost, lift the tuber, hose it clean, let it dry for several days, then store it in a jar of distilled water or in moist sand at around 50–55°F until spring. Done properly this saves a tropical lily year after year rather than buying again each season.
  • One of the strongest purples available in a tropical lily, and highly fragrant with it — the two do not always come together.
  • Blooms from June right through to frost, so the display runs the length of the season rather than peaking early.
  • Plant in a container rather than free into the pond bottom. It keeps the plant manageable and makes the autumn lift straightforward.
  • Attracts bees and dragonflies, which is worth having in a pond you want balanced.

New to planting water lilies? Read our complete Water Lily Planting Guide — tuber angle, soil, depth and the one mistake that kills most first lilies.

Notes

  • We don't ship dormant roots. Your tuber arrives fresh and actively growing with 1–2 young leaves already emerged — visible proof it's viable before it leaves us. Young pads may start fully submerged and will reach the surface within about a week in good light.
  • Remove yellowing pads and spent flowers as they appear to keep the water clean and push energy into new growth.
  • Never release aquatic plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Nymphaea Purple Joy | Purple & White Tropical Water Lily
products.body_html:
White petals tipped in purple. Nymphaea 'Purple Joy' is a tropical day-blooming water lily whose bicolour flowers open white and finish in vivid purple at the petal edges, around a golden-yellow centre. The blooms open with the sun and close at night, so the display changes through the day.

What You'll Receive

One young, viable Nymphaea 'Purple Joy' tuber with a healthy rhizome and 1–2 actively growing leaves, ensuring quick establishment and vigorous growth once planted.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Purple Joy Water Lily
  • Scientific name — Nymphaea 'Purple Joy'
  • Type — Tropical water lily, day-blooming; not winter-hardy
  • Flower — Bicolour: white petals brushed with vivid purple edges, golden-yellow centre; 5–7 inches across, lightly sweet scent
  • Foliage — Bright green floating pads
  • Bloom habit — Opens in sunlight, closes at night
  • Bloom season — Late spring through early fall
  • Placement — Ponds, patio containers and fountains; centrepiece

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Sunlight — Full sun, 6–8 hours of direct sunlight daily
  • Water — Best growth at 75–90°F
  • Water depth — 6–18 inches over the crown
  • Substrate — Rich loam or clay-based soil with aquatic fertiliser tablets
  • Planting angle — Tropical tuber: straight up at 90°, crown level with the soil
  • Overwintering — Not hardy. Lift before frost and store somewhere warm and frost-free through the cold months
  • Propagation — Tuber division, easiest when lifting for winter storage

Grower's Notes

  • The bicolour is the whole point, and it needs sun to show. The purple edging deepens with strong direct light; in a shaded pond the flowers open closer to plain white and lose the contrast that makes this cultivar worth choosing.
  • Day-blooming, so plan around it. Flowers open through the morning and close in the evening — this is a lily for a pond you see in daylight, not one you light at night.
  • Tropical means it will not survive a freeze. Lift the tuber before frost or treat it as an annual; leaving it in an icing pond is the usual way these are lost.
  • Wants genuine warmth. Growth is slow until the water reaches the mid-70s, then it moves quickly.
  • Broad pads shade the water, which limits algae and gives fish cover through summer.

New to planting water lilies? Read our complete Water Lily Planting Guide — tuber angle, soil, depth and the one mistake that kills most first lilies.

Notes

  • We don't ship dormant roots. Your tuber arrives fresh and actively growing with 1–2 young leaves already emerged — visible proof it's viable before it leaves us. Young pads may start fully submerged and will reach the surface within about a week in good light. Water lilies ship bare-root and should be planted on arrival.
  • Bloom and leaf colour, size and shape vary with lighting, water quality and plant maturity.
  • Never release aquatic plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Ludwigia Pantanal
products.body_html:
One of the most vividly coloured stem plants in the hobby, and one of the least tolerant. Ludwigia inclinata var. verticillata 'Pantanal' carries fine whorled leaves that run deep red into fiery orange — but only under strong light, CO₂ and steady feeding. From the Pantanal wetlands of South America. Grown emersed at our nursery.

What You'll Receive

Choose the format that suits your aquascaping needs:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approximately 6+ unrooted stems
  • Bunched Plants: 6+ fresh-cut stems without root bundled with foam and plant weight
  • Potted Plants: 6+ fresh-cut stems potted in rockwool within a 2-inch net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Ludwigia Pantanal
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia sp. 'Pantanal'
  • Also known as — Ludwigia inclinata var. verticillata 'Pantanal'
  • Origin — Pantanal wetlands, South America
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6+ fresh-cut stems, no roots
  • Mature height — 6–14 in
  • Suits — 20 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. High light is what produces the colour
  • CO₂ — Recommended, in practice near-essential for colour
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.0. Soft, low-carbonate water
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Green emersed, red submerged
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • It ships green and that is correct. Our nursery stock is emersed, with upright green stems and plain leaves. The red and orange appear only after several weeks of submerged growth under strong light — nothing has gone wrong in the first fortnight.
  • Soft water is not optional. Pantanal wants low carbonate hardness. In hard alkaline tap water it stunts at the tips whatever else you do — test KH rather than chasing a pH number.
  • This is the most demanding Ludwigia we sell. It reacts to swings in CO₂, photoperiod or dosing faster than almost any other stem plant, usually by dropping its lower leaves. Have the tank running steadily first.
  • Trim the tops and replant them — cuttings colour faster than the stumps regrow. Fine whorled leaves contrast strongly against broad-leaved plants, so use it where that difference shows.
  • Also available as sterile Ludwigia Pantanal Vitro Culture for a pest-free start.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Ludwigia Care Guide.

Notes

  • Ludwigia Pantanal requires high light, pressurized CO₂, and stable nutrient dosing to achieve its vibrant colouration and healthy growth. It is not suitable for low-tech setups. Emersed plants will arrive green and may undergo a transitional phase with some leaf melt before adapting to submerged growth.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Ludwigia Cuba
products.body_html:
A gradient rather than a single colour. Ludwigia inclinata var. verticillata 'Cuba' grows narrow leaves in symmetrical whorls that run yellow through orange to deep red on the same stem, with coppery new growth at the tips. From the Isla de la Juventud off Cuba, and one of the more striking stems in the genus when it is given what it wants.

Sold as loose fresh-cut plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Fresh Cut Plants: Approximately 6 individual, loose-cut stems without roots
  • Bunched Plants: Approximately 6 stems without roots, bundled with foam and a plant weight
  • Potted Plants: Approximately 6 stems without roots, potted in rockwool and net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Cuban Ludwigia
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia inclinata var. verticillata 'Cuba'
  • Also known as — Ludwigia sp. 'Cuba'
  • Origin — Isla de la Juventud, Cuba
  • Placement — Midground to background, planted in groups
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 emersed-grown stems, green on arrival
  • Mature height — 6–14 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Light intensity sets how far toward red it runs
  • CO₂ — Recommended for full colour and compact growth
  • Water — 64–86°F · pH 4.0–7.0 · KH 0–8. It takes genuinely soft, acidic water
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient substrate, plus iron and trace dosing
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Green oval leaves and yellow flowers when emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • Do not cut the base and hope. Unlike most stem plants, the lower portion left behind after a hard trim often deteriorates rather than reshooting. Cut the healthy tops, replant those, and pull the old bases — that is how this plant is maintained.
  • Green on arrival is correct. Emersed stock has plain green oval leaves and looks nothing like the photographs. The whorled form and the yellow-orange-red gradient develop over several weeks of submerged growth.
  • Iron is what pushes the red. Light gets it partway; consistent iron and trace dosing carries it the rest. Washed-out colour on a well-lit tank is almost always a micronutrient shortfall.
  • Soft water suits it — it tolerates down to pH 4.0 and very low KH, which makes it a good fit for a blackwater or RO-based tank where harder-water plants struggle.
  • Plant a group. The colour gradient reads properly across several stems together; a single stem just looks uncertain.

Notes

  • Colour intensity may vary depending on lighting, CO₂ levels, and nutrient availability. The plant may appear more green upon arrival and will gradually develop red and orange hues under proper aquarium conditions.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

The hairy Bacopa, marbled. Bacopa lanigera 'Variegata' keeps the soft hairs and slow, tidy growth of the species and adds cream-and-white variegation across the leaves. It stays compact, holds its shape without weekly trimming, and flowers purple when grown above water.

products.title: Ludwigia Tornado
products.body_html:
🌪️ Ludwigia Tornado — Twisted Red Stem Aquarium Plant

Ludwigia inclinata var. verticillata ‘Curly’, commonly known as Ludwigia Tornado or Ludwigia Twister, is one of the most visually striking stem plants in the aquarium hobby. Famous for its dramatic spiral-shaped leaves and vibrant reddish coloration, this rare aquatic plant creates intense movement and texture in planted aquariums. Under strong lighting and proper nutrients, Ludwigia Tornado develops tightly curled foliage with stunning shades of orange, red, and bronze that instantly become the centerpiece of any aquascape.

Ideal for experienced aquascapers, this unique Ludwigia species thrives in high-tech planted aquariums with stable CO₂ injection and nutrient-rich conditions.

🌟 Key Features

  • Scientific Name: Ludwigia inclinata var. verticillata ‘Curly’

  • Synonyms: Ludwigia Twister, Ludwigia Curly

  • Common Name: Ludwigia Tornado

  • Unique spiral and corkscrew leaf formation

  • Vibrant red, orange, and bronze coloration under high light

  • Excellent focal point for midground or background placement

🌱 Growth & Propagation

  • Growth Rate: Moderate

  • Placement: Midground / Background

  • Nutrient Substrate: Recommended

  • Can Be Grown Emersed: Yes

Ludwigia Tornado propagates easily through stem cuttings. Regular trimming encourages fuller growth and helps maintain its attractive compact shape. Stable water parameters and consistent nutrients are important to preserve its twisted leaf structure and vivid coloration.

🖼️ Aquascaping Benefits

  • Creates dramatic movement and texture with twisted foliage

  • Adds vibrant warm coloration to planted aquariums

  • Excellent contrast against green carpeting and moss species

📦 What You’ll Receive

Fresh, healthy Ludwigia Tornado cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®, available in convenient planting formats:

⚠️ Disclaimer

Aquarium plants are living organisms and may naturally vary in size, shape, and coloration depending on season, lighting, and growing conditions. Most plants are grown emersed before shipping and may transition in appearance after being introduced into submerged aquarium conditions.

products.title: Hydrocotyle Tripartita Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Clover leaves, in a carpet. Hydrocotyle tripartita — widely sold as Hydrocotyle 'Japan' — spreads fast across the foreground in tight clusters of small three-lobed leaves. It is one of the quickest carpets to establish and one of the easiest to shape with scissors. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format.

What You’ll Receive

  • One 4-inch Vitro Culture® bag of Hydrocotyle Tripartita ready to be rinsed, separated, and planted directly into your substrate.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Clover Plant, Hydrocotyle Japan
  • Scientific name — Hydrocotyle tripartita
  • Also known as — Hydrocotyle sp. 'Japan', Three-part Pennywort
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 2–4 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Light is what keeps it flat instead of climbing
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Nutrient substrate recommended
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Runners — cut and replant sections

Grower’s Notes

  • Light decides carpet or climber. Under strong light it hugs the substrate. Under weak light the runners stretch upward and it stops being a carpet — the single most common complaint about this plant, and it's a lighting problem, not a plant problem.
  • It grows fast enough to become a chore. Trim runners every few weeks or it crosses into neighbouring plants.
  • Pin fresh cuttings down with weights or tweezers until roots grab; loose sections float free.
  • Divide the tissue-culture portion into small clumps and plant them an inch apart rather than as one mass.
  • Compare with Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides — sturdier, thicker foliage, and quicker again.

Notes

  • Minor melting or yellowing may occur after planting while the plant adjusts to your tank conditions. With proper lighting and CO₂, new shoots and runners will appear rapidly.
  • Some aquatic plants are restricted in certain U.S. states — check before ordering, and never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.
